stories.title: Chandrashekhar sets sights on ‘cursed’ Hastinapur seat:4-election record links constituency winner to UP government formation
stories.summary: Hastinapur assembly seat in Uttar Pradesh has once again come into political focus amid speculation that Nagina MP Chandrashekhar may contest from the constituency. The development comes months after BJP MLA Dinesh Khatik publicly said he did not want to contest again from the seat, calling it “cursed”. Two months ago, speaking at a public event, Khatik said he did not want to become MLA from Hastinapur for the third time. He referred to a mythological belief linked to Draupadi and described the seat as “cursed”. Later, he clarified that he remained committed to serving the people of the constituency. Political observers say the seat has gained attention due to changing political signals, Chandrashekhar’s possible entry, and preparations by the Azad Samaj Party (ASP). Why Hastinapur seat is politically significant? Three key factors are being cited behind the speculation over Chandrashekhar contesting from Hastinapur. First, election results from the past four assembly polls show that the party winning this seat has gone on to form the government in Uttar Pradesh. This has strengthened the perception that the constituency holds symbolic and political importance. Second, Hastinapur is a reserved seat for Scheduled Castes. Such constituencies are considered important for Dalit leadership, and parties often field prominent candidates here to consolidate their support base. Third, Chandrashekhar, who won the Nagina Lok Sabha seat, is seen as trying to strengthen his political presence in western Uttar Pradesh. Contesting and winning from Hastinapur could help him demonstrate his grassroots support beyond social media and parliamentary politics. When asked about the possibility, Chandrashekhar said decisions on candidates and constituencies would be taken by the party leadership. He added that the Azad Samaj Party is preparing to contest all 403 assembly seats in the state. ASP begins groundwork, campaign visibility increases Azad Samaj Party leaders have started increasing political activity in Hastinapur. Wall paintings with Chandrashekhar’s name have appeared in key market areas, signalling an attempt to build public awareness. Hastinapur is part of the larger political region linked to the Nagina Lok Sabha constituency, from where Chandrashekhar was elected MP. His influence is already considered strong in the area, and party leaders are trying to expand that support ahead of the assembly elections. Recently, Chandrashekhar also appointed Ravindra Singh Bhati, a Gurjar leader and national general secretary of the party, as in-charge of the Meerut division. He has been given responsibility for Saharanpur, Moradabad, and Meerut divisions. Political observers see this move as an attempt to strengthen outreach among Gurjar voters, who play an important role in Hastinapur. Bhati has been associated with several Gurjar community mobilisations and is considered an influential regional leader. Experts say caste equations and political strategy will shape contest Senior journalist Pushpendra Sharma said the speculation around Chandrashekhar’s candidature may also be part of a broader political strategy in a Dalit-dominated seat. He noted that BJP MLA Dinesh Khatik had broken the trend by winning three consecutive elections from this reserved constituency. His recent remarks about not wanting to contest again could reflect growing opposition or anti-incumbency. Sharma added that the Samajwadi Party (SP) could benefit from changing political equations if multiple Dalit leaders contest and divide votes. He also said Chandrashekhar may be aiming to establish himself as a major Dalit leader at the state level by contesting from key reserved seats. However, he pointed out that it would be difficult for a sitting MP to resign and contest an assembly election unless it serves a clear political purpose. SP also focuses on seat, Gurjar vote remains crucial Senior journalist Rajesh Sharma said Hastinapur is politically significant not only because it is a reserved seat but also due to the influence of Gurjar voters. According to him, Gurjar voters often play a decisive role in determining the election outcome. He said Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has already held meetings with Gurjar leaders and organised conferences in Hastinapur, indicating the party’s focus on winning the seat. If Chandrashekhar contests, he is likely to face candidates from SP, BSP, and BJP. Political analysts believe this could divide Dalit votes and make the contest more competitive. BJP MLA’s statement adds to political uncertainty The political debate intensified after BJP MLA Dinesh Khatik’s earlier statement about not wanting to contest from Hastinapur. He made the remark at a school function, saying he did not wish to contest again from what he called a “cursed” seat. He later clarified that his statement was misunderstood and reaffirmed his commitment to serving the constituency. Political observers believe his remarks came at a time when opposition against him was growing locally and his candidature for the next election was uncertain. Seat likely to remain centre of political contest With Azad Samaj Party increasing its activity, Samajwadi Party strengthening its outreach, and uncertainty over BJP’s candidate, Hastinapur is expected to witness a closely contested election. Chandrashekhar’s final decision will depend on party strategy. However, the growing political mobilisation indicates that the reserved constituency will remain a key battleground in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.

stories.title: Latthmar Holi played in Barsana:Veiled women strike 'huriyars' with 'lathis', lakhs gather to watch | VIDEO
stories.summary: The traditional Latthmar Holi was celebrated in Barsana, Mathura, on Wednesday, drawing massive crowds from India and abroad. Women with veils covering their faces held sticks and playfully struck men from Nandgaon, known as huriyars, who defended themselves with shields. The vibrant celebration took place in Barsana’s famous Rangili Gali, where women symbolically chased and hit the huriyars as part of the centuries-old ritual. The men tried to protect themselves while singing and teasing, following the traditional customs linked to Lord Krishna and Radha. The festive atmosphere saw heavy participation, with around 20 lakh people reaching Mathura district to witness the unique Holi celebrations. Devotees, tourists, and locals gathered along the narrow lanes, rooftops, and balconies to watch the event. Police personnel were deployed in large numbers to manage the crowd and ensure safety. During the celebrations, women also playfully struck policemen with sticks, which is considered part of the festive spirit. Latthmar Holi in Barsana is one of the most famous Holi celebrations in India and is held every year ahead of the main Holi festival. The event reflects the cultural traditions of Braj and attracts visitors from across the country and overseas.

stories.title: Can Owaisi dent Akhilesh’s Muslim vote base in Uttar Pradesh?:BSP-AIMIM alliance could hurt SP; 7 seats lost due to vote split earlier
stories.summary: After its recent electoral gains in Bihar and Maharashtra, the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) has stepped up its political activity in Uttar Pradesh. The party’s national president Asaduddin Owaisi, along with his brother Akbaruddin Owaisi and state leaders, has begun targeting the Samajwadi Party (SP) and its chief Akhilesh Yadav. AIMIM leaders have openly challenged SP’s dominance among Muslim voters. Asaduddin Owaisi has also criticised Akhilesh Yadav and signalled the party’s intent to expand its base in Uttar Pradesh. This has raised questions about whether AIMIM can replicate its performance in Bihar and Maharashtra, and how much impact it could have on SP in future elections. AIMIM lacks the same ground presence as Bihar and Maharashtra Senior journalist Hasan Ejaz said AIMIM does not have the same organisational strength in Uttar Pradesh as it had in Bihar and Maharashtra. He explained that AIMIM’s success in Bihar was mainly limited to the Muslim-majority Seemanchal region, where the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) lacked strong Muslim leadership. He added that criticism of Owaisi by RJD leaders also created resentment among some Muslim voters, which helped AIMIM gain support. In Maharashtra, AIMIM’s growth was linked to local political conditions and internal divisions within other parties. Its success was mainly seen in municipal corporation elections rather than parliamentary polls. SP has strong Muslim representation across Uttar Pradesh Political observers say the Samajwadi Party has a wide network of Muslim leaders across Uttar Pradesh. SP has influential leaders in most districts, especially in western Uttar Pradesh and eastern regions. Prominent SP Muslim leaders include Ikra Hasan, Shahid Manzoor, Qadir Rana, ST Hasan, Azam Khan, Mohibulla Nadvi, Rafiq Ansari, Iqbal Mahmood, Mahboob Ali and Ziaurrahman Barq in western Uttar Pradesh. In other regions, leaders such as Afzal Ansari in Ghazipur, Ziauddin Rizvi in Ballia and Zahid Beg in Bhadohi remain key faces. Analysts say this widespread representation makes it difficult for AIMIM to quickly build a strong base in the state. AIMIM contested 95 seats in 2022 but failed to win any In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, AIMIM contested 95 seats but did not win any. The party secured about 0.5 percent of the total vote share and received around 4.5 lakh votes. Its best performance was in Mubarakpur, where it received 36,460 votes. However, the Samajwadi Party won the seat by a margin of about 29,000 votes. In Sambhal, AIMIM secured more than 20,000 votes, but SP still won comfortably. AIMIM’s weakest performance was in Thanabhawan in Shamli district, where it received only 325 votes. Despite not winning any seats, AIMIM affected the outcome in several constituencies. In seven seats, the number of votes secured by AIMIM candidates was higher than SP’s margin of defeat. Of the 95 seats contested by AIMIM, BJP and its allies won 51 seats, while SP and its allies won 44. SP taking a cautious approach unlike RJD Unlike RJD in Bihar, which openly criticised AIMIM, the Samajwadi Party has taken a cautious approach. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has avoided direct confrontation with AIMIM and has reportedly advised party spokespersons to remain restrained on the issue. Political observers say SP’s Muslim-Yadav support base and its broader social coalition strategy remain key strengths in Uttar Pradesh. Shaukat Ali leading AIMIM’s expansion in Uttar Pradesh AIMIM’s state president Shaukat Ali is the party’s main face in Uttar Pradesh. He has been holding meetings in various districts to strengthen the organisation. Shaukat Ali has announced that AIMIM will contest district panchayat elections and the 2027 Assembly elections across all 75 districts of the state. The party is also relying on the leadership of Asaduddin Owaisi and Akbaruddin Owaisi to attract voters. He has accused the Samajwadi Party of ignoring Muslim interests and said AIMIM will offer an alternative political platform. Possible impact if AIMIM and BSP align Senior journalist Syed Kasim said AIMIM could have a greater impact if it forms an alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). Such a coalition could attract both Muslim and Dalit voters and create challenges for SP. However, BSP chief Mayawati has said her party will contest future elections independently and has not announced any alliance plans. Limited impact so far, but expansion plans continue Political analysts say AIMIM currently lacks the organisational strength and leadership network in Uttar Pradesh compared to SP. However, its presence could influence results in closely contested seats by affecting vote distribution. The party is focusing on expanding its base ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Its future impact will depend on its ability to build local leadership, form alliances and gain sustained voter support.

stories.title: UP’s ‘Super cop’ accused of conspiracy by Shankaracharya:IPS officer known for 500 encounters, who once jailed Ashutosh Brahmachari
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand has accused IPS officer Dr Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring with Ashutosh Brahmachari, who had filed a case against him. The Shankaracharya also released a photograph showing Sharma cutting a cake with Brahmachari, alleging it indicates a close association between the two. He claimed that the officer, known for handling encounter cases, was behind what he described as a “script” leading to his arrest. According to the Shankaracharya, the officer played a key role in the developments that resulted in legal action against him. However, records show that Sharma had earlier taken action against Ashutosh Brahmachari. While serving as Superintendent of Police in Shamli, he had arrested Brahmachari and sent him to jail in connection with a separate case. Dr Ajay Pal Sharma joined the Indian Police Service in 2011 after training as a dentist. He is widely known as an encounter specialist and has been involved in more than 500 encounters during his career. Police data indicates that 15 accused were killed in these encounters, while several others were arrested. No official response from Sharma or the police department has been issued so far regarding the Shankaracharya’s allegations. 136 encounters in 22 months Dr. Ajay Pal Sharma from Ludhiana, Punjab was a dental surgeon before becoming an IPS officer. He obtained his BDS (Dental Sciences) degree from Government Medical College, Patiala. His younger brother Amit Pal Sharma is an IAS officer. 41-year-old Ajay Pal is currently posted as Additional CP (Law and Order) in Prayagraj. Prior to this, he has served as SP/SSP in five districts. During his 22-month tenure as SP in Jaunpur, he conducted a record 136 encounters. This is the highest number of encounters during any SP's tenure in any district. Commanded these districts He has served as captain of Hathras, Shamli, Ghaziabad, Rampur and Jaunpur. In 2013, he was posted as ASP in the Kumbh Mela organized in Prayagraj. He was also given responsibility as SP Personnel and captain of UP-112 at police headquarters. Woman had made serious allegations Ajay Pal Sharma's career was not only filled with successes but also controversies. In 2020, a woman named Deepti Sharma made serious allegations against him. The woman claimed that Ajay Pal had married her in 2016 and later backed out. This case became so big that an FIR was filed against them at Hazratganj police station in Lucknow and an SIT investigation was also set up. Due to this controversy, their promotion remained stalled for a long time, though they later received a clean chit. Served as Nodal Officer in Mahakumbh Just before Mahakumbh, he was posted as Nodal Officer (Mahakumbh, Commissionerate Prayagraj) in Prayagraj. On December 22, 2024, he was made Additional CP Prayagraj. During this time, he played an important role in the successful organization of Mahakumbh. After Mahakumbh, he was given the responsibility of Additional CP (Law and Order) Prayagraj. Ajay Pal's name was not in Shankaracharya's initial allegations Ajay Pal Sharma was also present there along with other officers during the dispute at Sangam Ghat on Mauni Amavasya. In the crowd of officers, he was seen at the forefront with a loudspeaker repeatedly requesting Shankaracharya and his supporters to clear the path for coming and going. Although after Mauni Amavasya, Shankaracharya presented his views on the controversy in a press conference on January 19. He showed the names and photos of district officials, which did not include Dr. Ajay Pal Sharma's name. Ajay Pal was posted in Shamli for about one and a half years Ajay Pal Sharma was appointed as SP Shamli by the then SP government on October 17, 2016. He remained posted until March 2018. Ashutosh Pandey alias Ashutosh Brahmachari is a history-sheeter from Kandla police station in Shamli. He has 21 cases registered against him. It was Ajay Pal Sharma who had sent Ashutosh Brahmachari to jail. Additional CP Law and Order IPS Dr. Ajay Pal Sharma said- The case has been registered on court's orders. Investigation is being conducted impartially. Further action will be taken based on the evidence that comes forward. Declined to comment on the allegations made by Shankaracharya.

stories.title: Woman cheated of ₹2.20 lakh in fake house sale deal:Beware of fraud while buying or selling a property; 7 things you must know
stories.summary: Recently, a woman was reportedly cheated out of ₹2.20 lakh by a man who promised to sell her a house in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. According to the police report, the man took an advance payment of ₹30,000 and later collected the remaining amount. However, he neither transferred the house to her name nor returned the money. When the woman asked for her money back, the man allegedly threatened her. Following a complaint from the woman’s son, the police are investigating the matter. Such property fraud incidents highlight the issues people usually face while buying or selling property. While buying a home is a significant challenge, selling an old house can be equally complicated. Sellers often struggle to get a fair price for their property, while buyers sometimes become victims of fraud or overcharges. Therefore, it’s crucial to be cautious. If you are planning to sell your house for the first time, here’s what you need to know: Expert Insight: Ayush Dubey, Broker Associate, Bhopal When you are buying a property Buying a property requires patience, research, and legal caution. Rushing to make a decision can lead to financial loss, while careful planning can secure a safe and profitable investment. So, before you buy the house, first do better planning, take care of all your needs like- Legal documentation checklist is the most important To avoid fraud and any kind of false trap, keep all legal and financial matters clear. Gather complete information with the agent and seller and verify the ownership. Also take care of these things- When you are selling a house Everyone wants to sell their property at a good price. However, getting the right value can feel like an uphill task. First, you publish s, then choose the right real estate website, upload photos and videos, search for buyers, and arrange multiple property visits. After considerable effort, you may finally find a serious buyer. Even then, many sellers fail to secure a good deal. The main reason behind this is lack of proper planning, research, and preparation. Without prior experience, the process becomes even more challenging. How to plan properly before selling a house? Selling a house is a lengthy and exhausting process. Smart planning is crucial. Focus on these important aspects: How to decide the right price as per market rate? Most sellers feel their property is being undervalued and expect a higher price than market standards. Therefore, the first step is to determine the correct selling price. According to broker associate Ayush Dubey, knowing the market rate is essential. The price should neither be too high nor too low compared to prevailing rates. Ways to determine market rate: After gathering this information, set your price. If you are quoting above market value, you must have valid reasons, such as: How to choose the right broker or real estate agent? Finding a trustworthy agent is a major task. To avoid fraud and secure a better deal: Research the agent: Check property s in newspapers to find local agents. Ask acquaintances about their reputation. Check track record: Speak to friends or relatives who recently bought or sold property and learn from their experiences. Verify credentials: Check online reviews and verify credentials. You may even verify records through local authorities to avoid fraud. How to prepare the house before showing it to buyers? The condition of your house significantly impacts its value. No matter how valuable the property is, if it looks unclean or poorly maintained, its perceived market value drops. Remember, first impressions matter. Before listing your house: Do photos and videos affect sales? Yes, significantly. Along with factual details, the quality of photos and videos on property websites strongly influences buyer interest. Documents required when selling a house Before selling, gather all necessary documents in one file: Legal and Financial Transparency Keep all legal and financial matters clear. Share complete information with the agent and buyer. Do not hide disputes, ongoing legal cases, home loans, or pending dues. Trying to be “smart” can backfire later. How to beware of property fraud while buying or selling a house? Property fraud cases, like the Moradabad incident, highlight the need for caution. Take care of these points- Careful planning, proper documentation, and market research can protect you from financial loss and legal trouble while buying or selling a house.

stories.title: Stray dogs maul 8-year-old girl to death in Lucknow:Body found 500 meters away from house in a field, flesh hanging
stories.summary: Stray dogs killed an 8-year-old girl by mauling her in Lucknow. The blood-soaked body of the girl was found in a field about 500 meters away from home. Her face was completely mutilated. Pieces of flesh were hanging from various places. The incident occurred around 6 PM on Sunday in Tarauna village of the Rahimabad police station area. The deceased was identified as Anshika. She was a class 1 student. She had left home alone when the dogs attacked her. Some women from Tarauna village had gone towards the fields in the evening. During this time, they saw someone lying on the ground in the field. The women got scared and came to the village to tell people about this. Upon receiving the information, villagers reached the field with sticks. The villagers saw that Anshika's blood-soaked body was lying in the field. Dogs were sitting in a pack at some distance The villagers said that after this, we informed Anshika's family members about this. The family members reached the spot and brought the body home with our help. They also informed the police. The villagers said that where Anshika's body was lying, fierce dogs were sitting at some distance from there. Those dogs were from the neighboring village. Face badly mauled, flesh torn apart Villagers said that no one saw when the dogs were mauling the girl. But looking at the girl's body, it's clear that she was attacked by dogs. There were marks of dog bites on the girl's face. Her face was completely mauled. Pieces of flesh were torn out in several places. There were dog paw prints at the spot where the body was found. Anshika was the youngest among 3 siblings Anshika was the youngest of three children of her parents. Her father, Dilip Kashyap, said that Anshika had left home in the evening. A while later, they received news of her death. Mother Soni fainted upon seeing the body. Other family members are also in terrible condition, crying continuously.

Saharanpur man kills friend to fake his own death:Body burnt in car as part of plan to dodge rape case
stories.summary: A young man killed his friend to fake his own death in Saharanpur. He placed the body in a car, poured petrol, and set it on fire. The accused did this to escape punishment in a rape case. After the incident, the accused fled to Dehradun. To hide his identity, the main accused got his hair cut. He got a new SIM card and called his brother to file a missing person report, so that police would consider him dead. The brother filed the missing person report. On February 25, a burnt body was found in an Alto car near the Kali River in Amrapur forest by the roadside. When police investigated, the case was uncovered. On February 28, four people, including the main accused, were arrested. During interrogation, the accused confessed to their crime. The case belongs to the Gagalhedi police station area. SSP Abhinandan said that on February 25, the village head of Chaurakhurd informed the police that a burnt Alto car was standing near a culvert on the Chandpur road. In which there was a burnt body of a person. The police and the field unit reached the spot and started an investigation. The car was identified based on its burnt number. Investigation revealed that the car had been sold multiple times. The young man named Arjun had last purchased it on February 16, 2026. Meanwhile, Arjun's brother Vijay Sagar reached the police station and informed that Arjun has been missing since February 24. His phone is switched off. Police started the investigation. Meanwhile, on February 27, Babita, a resident of Mohammadpur Kandhela village, reached the police station with her son Akshay and other family members. She said that my son Rohit has been missing for 5 days. Arjun, whose body was found in the car, was Rohit's friend. He used to visit his house. DNA test revealed the body was Rohit's Babita had told the police that Rohit had borrowed ₹1.60 lakh from Arjun. Which he was unable to repay. Police became suspicious. Police intensified the investigation. Police conducted a DNA test on the dead body found in the car. DNA matched with the family members. The dead body found in the car was Rohit's. Police handed over the body to the family. Now police started searching for Arjun. Police began monitoring Vijay Sagar, the brother who had filed Arjun's missing report. The number was put under surveillance. Meanwhile, it was discovered that Arjun was alive. He was living in Dehradun. On February 28, Arjun came to meet his younger brother Vijay Sagar. Police arrested both of them near the Badkala flyover. Now read the accused's confession... When the police interrogated him, Arjun told the truth. Arjun said - In 2024, I raped a minor in Dehradun. I went to jail in that case. I was afraid that I might get sentenced. So I made a plan to fake my death to escape. In jail, I met Sarik. He was imprisoned in a kidnapping case. Friendship with Rohit began in July 2025 A year later, I got out of jail on bail. Then I started working at a private finance company in Jhabreda. During this time in July, I became friends with Rohit. I got him addicted to alcohol. Then I lent him about ₹1.60 lakh. After this, on the night of February 24, I took Rohit with me. My other companions, Robin and Sarik, were also with me. We made Rohit drink alcohol. When he was intoxicated, we strangled him to death with a muffler. After this, we placed the body on the driver's seat of the Alto car, poured petrol, and set it on fire. So that it would appear that Arjun died in an accident. Police have recovered a Kia Sonet car from the accused.

stories.title: ‘No action for cows, we will launch religious fight’:Shankaracharya adds, 'Yogi not proving himself to be Hindu'
stories.summary: ‘40 days time was given, 30 days have passed, but Yogi has not proved himself as a true Hindu. No effort has been made for ’Gau Mata'. Therefore, we will have to declare a religious war for the dignity of 'Gau Mata'. We will have to draw a line to see who is in favour of the cow and who is against it.' It has become necessary that after 40 days, on the 41st day, we should go to Lucknow and announce the beginning of the religious war for the dignity of ‘Gau Mata’. In the remaining 10 days, there will be a final wait of hope. After that, on March 11, after the period of 40 days is over, it will be necessary to make the announcement.' Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand said this while targeting CM Yogi. He said that from March 11, they will declare a religious war in Lucknow to declare ‘Gau Mata’ as the national mother. Regarding Israel and America's attack on Iran, Shankaracharya said that when hypocrisy increases, such wars happen. If there is a religious war, there will be no need for such physical wars. We responded in 12 hours; they couldn't respond even in 30 days Shankaracharya said - We were asked to explain within 24 hours how we could call ourselves Shankaracharya? We answered in 12 hours. After that, to investigate whether some 'Kalnemi' have entered our society. We had asked Adityanath ji, who is handling the responsibility of the Chief Minister wearing saffron clothes, to explain how you are a real Hindu. Tell us in 40 days. When 10 days passed, we assessed whether these people did anything in these 10 days or not. When 20 days passed, we assessed again. Today, after 30 days have passed, we have again assessed whether they have gained any clarity about being Hindu. Have they done anything about the demand of the country's Sanatani people regarding ‘Gau Mata’? Sadly, 30 days have passed, and so far, no such effort has been seen from their side for ‘Gau Mata’. Yes, during this time, Yogi was abroad for almost a week. Now, he can say that I wasn't even here. However, you cannot make excuses to go abroad by ignoring the sentiments of the majority of people in your country. Therefore, it has been confirmed that no effort was made by them. Read what he said about the America-Israel and Iran issue Shankaracharya said - Wars keep happening all the time. Sometimes with weapons, sometimes for power balance. Every country keeps making plans against the others. But just because there's a war somewhere, should we abandon protecting our dharma? Should we give permission to slaughter and eat cows because war has broken out? Sell them, satisfy the British. Cut up our mother cow and serve it to them. This is why our ancestors participated in the freedom struggle to drive out the British. So that when they leave, we can slaughter cows and send them. This is such a despicable thing. This war is happening because religious wars have stopped. When there is religious war, people will have respect for religion in their minds. The hypocrisy that is happening in the name of religion will end. Such wars happen when hypocrisy increases. The President of America says that we should get the Nobel Peace Prize. He also makes all the arrangements for war. This is hypocrisy. When such hypocrisy spreads in the world. When hypocrisy is not controlled, such wars happen. Therefore, religious war is very necessary, so that such material wars do not happen. People should not suffer loss of life and property. We do not wish for peace; let the heat come out, so that peace happens automatically. Therefore, let it happen. Read the latest case of ongoing controversy regarding Shankaracharya in detail There was a dispute between Shankaracharya and the administration on Mauni Amavasya on January 18 at the Prayagraj Magh Mela. 8 days later, on January 24, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya's disciple Ashutosh Maharaj filed a complaint with the Police Commissioner. In this, allegations of sexual exploitation of children were made during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025. A petition was filed in the Special POCSO Court on February 8, alleging inaction by the police. On February 13, 2 children were presented in court. Their statements were recorded on February 21. On the court's orders, an FIR was registered at Jhunsi police station the same day. Shankaracharya, his disciple Mukundanand, and 2-3 unknown persons were named as accused in the FIR. On February 24, Shankaracharya accused Prayagraj Additional Commissioner Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring against him. He also filed an anticipatory bail petition in the Allahabad High Court. On the 27th, the High Court granted bail to Shankaracharya.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:US, Israel dropped 1,200 bombs on Iran within 24hrs; UP village linked to Khamenei’s legacy more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. US, Israel dropped 1,200 bombs on Iran within 24hrs The Israeli Air Force said it dropped more than 1,200 bombs on Iran over the past day in joint strikes with the United States, including the attack that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. 2. BLO found hanging in Fatehpur school; denied leave for daughter’s wedding A Shikshamitra working as a Booth Level Officer (BLO) for SIR duty in Fatehpur allegedly died by suicide inside the school where he was posted. The incident came to light around 5 PM on Saturday. According to reports, the school peon found him hanging from a noose in a classroom and immediately alerted the family and police. 3. UP village linked to Khamenei’s legacy; mentor’s roots traced to Barabanki After reports of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s death, a village in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh, has drawn attention for its historical link to Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khamenei. Residents of Kintur village claim Khamenei’s ancestors belonged to their village and were known in Iran as “Musavi Hindi.” Locals say several descendants later moved to Iran and contributed to religious and social developments there. 4. Mob attacks US embassy in Pak’s Karachi, 12 dead The United States and Israel continued airstrikes on Iran for the second consecutive day, intensifying tensions across the Middle East. Iran has reportedly retaliated with strikes targeting US military bases in Israel and across nine countries in the region. 5. Protests in Lucknow after Khamenei’s death; Shia community raises slogans Following the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an attack by the United States and Israel, protests erupted in Uttar Pradesh. In Lucknow, thousands from the Shia community took to the streets. Women were seen crying and beating their chests as protesters raised slogans of “Khamenei Zindabad” and “Down with America and Israel.” 6. Attackers flee to Delhi after slitting YouTuber Saleem Wastik’s throat YouTuber Saleem Wastik from Loni on the Delhi-Ghaziabad border is battling for his life after two unidentified attackers entered his house and slit his throat. He is admitted to Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital in Delhi with multiple knife wounds and remains in critical condition. CCTV footage tracked the attackers for about 2.5 km before they fled towards Delhi. 7. 17 killed in blast at Nagpur's detonator manufacturing company A massive explosion occurred on Sunday, 1 March 2026, at SBL Energy Limited, an ammunition manufacturing company located in Raulgaon, Katol taluka of Nagpur, Maharashtra. In this explosion, 17 workers were killed, and 18 were injured. Many of the injured are in critical condition. 8. 7-year-old Vaishnavi dies of burns in Lucknow; village mourns A wave of grief swept a Barabanki village after seven-year-old Vaishnavi, who had suffered 60% burns, died after a week at Lucknow’s trauma centre. Just days before Holi, her body was brought home for the last rites. Villagers gathered in the narrow lanes in tears, praying that no family should face such tragedy. 9. March likely to bring intense heat wave; temperature may touch 40°C Winter officially ends on March 1, but this year rising temperatures are already raising concerns. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), March could be among the warmest months on record, with temperatures in Uttar Pradesh likely to touch 40°C and the summer expected to be harsher than last year. 10. Banks will not operate for 18 days in March 2026 In March 2026, banks will not operate for a total of 18 days in different states across the country. stories.title: Wife murdered by strangulation, body dumped in drain:Husband deletes CCTV footage to escape crime; had love marriage 5 years ago
stories.summary: A 28-year-old woman was allegedly murdered by her husband in Kanpur, who strangled her to death and dumped the body in a drain to destroy evidence. According to police, the accused wrapped the body of his wife, Akriti Singh alias Ruby, in a blanket and threw it into a drain located about 500 metres from their house in Saraimeeta area of Panki. He also placed stones on the body to prevent it from floating and to conceal the crime. Body spotted in drain, police informed The incident came to light on Saturday morning when passersby noticed a human head in the drain and immediately alerted the police. Officers reached the spot, recovered the body and sent it to the mortuary for post-mortem examination. Later that night, Akriti’s brother identified the body and confirmed her identity to the police. See 2 images- Love marriage five years ago Police said Akriti had married the accused in a temple five years ago after a love relationship. The couple had been living together in the Panki area since then. Initial investigation suggests there were ongoing domestic disputes between the couple, which eventually led to the murder. Husband and two relatives arrested Police have arrested the accused husband along with his two brothers, who are suspected of helping him dispose of the body. All three are currently being interrogated. During questioning, the husband confessed to strangling his wife. CCTV footage deleted to hide evidence Investigators also discovered that CCTV footage from the house had been deliberately deleted in an apparent attempt to destroy evidence and mislead the investigation. Police said further questioning and forensic examination are underway, and additional legal action will follow based on the findings. Frequent fights over jewellery worth lakhs, says victim’s brother The victim’s brother said Akriti had married Nitin of her own choice five years ago, and the family had supported the marriage. She regularly visited her maternal home, where their mother had given her jewellery worth several lakhs. According to the brother, Akriti would wear the jewellery during family functions but would later return it to her maternal home for safekeeping. However, her husband Nitin often objected to this and insisted she bring the jewellery back with her. When Akriti refused, he would question her decision. She reportedly told him she feared he might sell the jewellery and spend the money, which led to frequent arguments between the couple. Police mediation on February 26, murder committed after returning home The brother further revealed that Nitin had assaulted Akriti on February 26. Following the assault, Akriti approached the Panki Temple police post and filed a complaint. Police called both Akriti and Nitin to the police post and facilitated a compromise between them. After the mediation, the couple returned home. However, later that same day, Nitin allegedly assaulted Akriti again. He then strangled her to death, wrapped her body in a blanket, and dumped it in a drain located about 500 metres from their house. He also placed stones over the body to prevent it from floating and to conceal the crime. Body found in drain, police alerted by passersby On the morning of February 28, passersby noticed a body in the drain and immediately informed police by calling the emergency helpline number 112. Police from Panki police station reached the spot and recovered the body. Initial attempts to identify the victim were unsuccessful, and the body was sent to the mortuary. Later, family members identified the deceased as Akriti Singh alias Ruby, after which police intensified the investigation and arrested the accused husband and his relatives. Police conducting postmortem today Late Saturday night when family members got information about the incident through social media, they contacted Panki police. When police showed the photo to brother Rahul, he identified the body as his sister Akriti Singh aka Ruby. Today on Sunday, police are conducting the postmortem. After postmortem, police will hand over the body to Akriti's family. Then the last rites will be performed. Husband Confessed - Murdered by Strangulation Police arrested the accused husband Nitin Savita, brother-in-law Deepu and Rahul late Saturday night. Father-in-law Suresh Master was also taken into custody but was released due to poor health. DCP MS Kasim Abdi said- The accused are being interrogated. The accused husband has confessed to murdering by strangulation and disposing of the body. Accused Deleted Home CCTV Footage DCP said - Action will be taken based on the complaint from the maternal family. How did he take the body from house to drain? Did anyone else help in this? What was the main reason for murder... investigation is ongoing on these and other points. The accused has deleted the footage from home CCTV cameras. Footage from other nearby cameras is being examined.

stories.title: Boyfriend Ends Life After Girlfriend’s Death in UP's Sultanpur:Leaves note saying 'life meaningless without her'; couple buried together
stories.summary: A lover committed suicide after his girlfriend's death in UP's Sultanpur. Both were in a relationship for 3 years. The girlfriend died in a road accident on the afternoon of February 25. Upon hearing the news, the young man was heartbroken. He reached her home to see her one last time and learned that she had been buried. The young man named Vineet went straight to the cemetery. He started digging the grave. When people present there stopped him, he left and never returned. Two days later, on February 28, his body was found hanging in a garden. The family buried him near his girlfriend's grave. Meanwhile, Vineet's Instagram post has come into light. It said “Hello brothers this is my last video. What will I live for now when my life is no longer in this world. Please forgive me brothers, bye". Understand entire step by step sequence of events Vineet (25), a resident of Ghatampur, was the youngest of three brothers. He had studied till fourth grade. His father died 5 years ago. He met Arpita in a clothing store where they both used to work and gradually fell in love. According to Vineet's brother Swamitt, Arpita died in a road accident on February 25. She had gone to the market with her brother, where a car hit their bike. Swamitt said “When Vineet learned about Arpita's death the next day, he was shocked. He went to her house to see Arpita for the last time. There he fainted while crying. Then we brought him back home”. Vineet was very disturbed after Arpita's death According to Vineet's sister in law Kajal “He was very disturbed since Arpita's death and stopped eating and drinking. He wasn't talking to anyone. He went there again in the evening. Found out that she had been buried. After this, he went to Arpita's grave where he started digging her grave”. She further added “When people stopped him, he ran away. Then he didn't return. He was searched extensively but couldn't be found. After this, we filed a missing person report for Vineet at the police station”. Police found Vineet's location in a garden After the filing of missing report police searched for Vineet for two days but couldn't find him. Police tried to trace his phone where his location was found in a garden 8 km away from the village. When family members and police reached there, they found his body hanging. Police found a love letter from his pocket Police lowered the body and searched the surroundings. Police also found a love letter from his pocket. After this, the body was sent for post-mortem. On Saturday evening, after the post-mortem, the body came home and family members performed the last rites and his body was buried right next to Arpita's grave.

stories.title: How a UP village shaped Khamenei’s legacy:Supreme Leader's mentor had roots in Barabanki, known as 'Musavi Hindi' in Iran
stories.summary: After reports of the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, a village in Uttar Pradesh’s Barabanki district has come into the spotlight due to its claimed historical connection with Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khomeini. Residents of Kintur village say that the ancestors of Ruhollah Khomeini, who led Iran’s 1979 Islamic Revolution, belonged to their village. Locals claim that several descendants of this village later went to Iran and played a role in religious and social developments there. According to villagers, people from Barabanki used to travel to Iran on religious pilgrimages during the time of the Nawabs. They also say that Syed Ahmad Musavi, the grandfather of Ruhollah Khomeini, lived in Kintur village during the 18th and early 19th centuries before moving abroad. Following the news of Khamenei’s death, Syed Nihal Miyan, who claims to be a descendant of Khomeini and lives in Kintur, expressed deep sorrow. He said Khamenei stood for humanity beyond religion and community, and his death was a great loss. Another local resident, Dr Rehan Kazmi, described Khamenei’s death in the Israeli attack as “martyrdom” and called it an irreparable loss. Khomeini’s grandfather had roots in Barabanki According to local accounts and historical references, Syed Ahmad Musavi, the grandfather of Ruhollah Khomeini, was born in Kintur village in the early 19th century. The village has long been known as a centre of Shia Islamic learning. In 1830, Syed Ahmad Musavi left British India on a religious journey to Najaf, a major Shia religious centre in present-day Iraq. He later settled in Najaf and eventually moved to the Iranian city of Khomein. To preserve his Indian identity, he added the word “Hindi” to his name and became known as Syed Ahmad Musavi Hindi. Iranian records still mention this name. He later bought a house in Iran and married Sakineh. The couple had four children, including a son whose descendants later included Ruhollah Khomeini, the architect of Iran’s Islamic Revolution. Today, residents of Kintur village say this historical link remains a matter of pride and has once again drawn attention after the reported death of Iran’s Supreme Leader. Religious influence and heritage linked to Musavi family The Musavi family, to which Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khomeini belonged, is believed to be descended from the seventh Shia Imam, Imam Musa al-Kazim. Because of this lineage, the family held a respected position in Shia religious circles and was known for its spiritual leadership. Syed Ahmad Musavi, Khomeini’s grandfather, played an important role in preserving this religious legacy. He later settled in the Middle East and died in Karbala in 1869. His teachings and ideology continued to influence his family and future generations, including Ruhollah Khomeini. Even today, villagers in Kintur claim that descendants of Khomeini’s family continue to live in the ancestral house in Barabanki, maintaining the historical and cultural connection between the village and Iran. The Iranian revolution of 1979 and Khomeini’s leadership In 1979, Ruhollah Khomeini led the Islamic Revolution in Iran, which ended the rule of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and established Iran as an Islamic Republic. Following the revolution, Khomeini became the country’s Supreme Leader. Despite holding the highest position of power, Khomeini was known for his simple lifestyle. He lived in a modest single-storey house and reportedly avoided using public funds for personal comfort. His leadership and ideology played a major role in shaping modern Iran’s political and religious structure. Rise of Ali Khamenei after Khomeini’s death Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was born on July 17, 1939, in Mashhad, Iran. Inspired by Khomeini’s teachings, he actively participated in the Islamic Revolution and became one of Khomeini’s trusted associates. After Khomeini’s death in 1989, Khamenei was appointed as Iran’s Supreme Leader. He remained in this position for decades, becoming one of the most influential figures in Iran’s political and religious system. While Khamenei himself did not have direct links with India, his mentor Khomeini’s ancestral roots in Uttar Pradesh have continued to attract attention. Historical importance of Kintur village in Barabanki Kintur village in Uttar Pradesh’s Barabanki district holds historical significance due to its claimed connection with Syed Ahmad Musavi. From this village, Musavi travelled abroad and eventually settled in Iran, where his descendants went on to influence the country’s history. Several Shia families in the village still recall their ancestral links to Iran. Syed Nihal Kazmi, a 70-year-old resident, claims that his great-grandfather, Mufti Mohammad Quli Musavi, and Syed Ahmad Musavi were cousins. Locals say this connection remains an important part of the village’s identity, and recent developments in Iran have once again brought attention to Kintur’s historical and religious heritage.

stories.title: Lord Krishna plays Holi in Mathura's Gokul:Rides in a palaki from Nand Bhavan to Murlighat, chants of 'Jai Radhe Jai Krishna' echoes.
stories.summary: The atmosphere has turned festive in Braj with people immersed in celebration of Holi with their beloved Lord Krishna. Folk songs are being sung in every home and the temples are echoing with the chants of “Jai Radhe Jai Krishna”. On Sunday (March 1st), people gathered to celebrate Holi with Lord Krishna's form in Gokul. They have brought abir, colors and sticks with them and are accompanied by their family members and friends. Lord Krishna played ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ marking the beginning of the festivities The palaki ride emerged from Nand Bhavan, where Lord Krishna in his child form was seated in his palaki. From here the palaki reached to Murlidhar Ghat where it is believed that Lord played flute for the first time. At the ghat Lord Krishna played ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ (Holi with sticks) with the Gopis, marking the beginning of Holi celebrations in Gokul. ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ is celebrated in memory of Lord Krishna's childhood form and his divine plays. This festival is specially celebrated keeping the image of ‘Bal Gopal’ (child form of Lord Krishna) at the center. Therefore, small sticks called ‘Chhari’ are used instead of large sticks called ‘Lath’.

stories.title: ‘Only death will free me from SIR’:BLO found hanging in Fatehpur school; wrote he was denied leave for daughter’s wedding
stories.summary: A Shikshamitra, who was working as a Booth Level Officer (BLO) for SIR duty in Fatehpur, allegedly died by suicide inside the school where he was posted. The incident came to light on Saturday evening around 5 PM. According to information, the school peon saw the teacher hanging from a noose inside a classroom. He immediately raised an alarm and informed the family members as well as the police. Police reached the school soon after. The classroom door was open, and the teacher was found hanging inside. He was taken down and rushed to a nearby hospital, but doctors declared him dead. During the initial investigation, police found a suicide note kept on the teacher’s table. Further inquiry is underway.. It read: I am fed up with work. My daughter's wedding is on March 8th. I am not getting leave. That's why I am committing suicide. After dying, I will be free from SIR. After the teacher's death, villagers and family members created a ruckus at the hospital. Upon receiving this information, officials arrived and somehow pacified the family. After this, the body was sent for a post-mortem. The case is from the Bindki Kotwali area. ADM Avinash Tripathi stated: The suicide note that was found will be investigated. Further action will be taken after the post-mortem report is received. First, read the BLO's suicide note I, Akhilesh Kumar, am fed up with the BLO's work. For this work, I made rounds of officers, SDM and EO sir. My daughter is getting married. I said that someone else should be assigned the duty, but no officer or employee was willing to listen. The event is on March 8. Despite having so much work, I am continuously doing the BLO's work. My household chores remained incomplete. How much work can I, a single person, do? Distressed by this, I have been forced to take my own life. The Election Commission is responsible for me and my family. After my death, I will be freed from SIR. Taught children all day, found hanging in the evening In Aliabad village, Akhilesh Savita (50) lived with his wife Manju Devi, daughter Divyanshi (20), and son Divyansh. Akhilesh was a Shikshamitra (para-teacher) at the village's primary school. He was deployed for BLO work in SIR. His daughter Divyanshi's wedding was scheduled for March 8. He was asking for leave for this. It is alleged that he was not getting leave. On Saturday, he reached school at 9 AM. He taught the children. The children were dismissed at 3 PM. After this, he started doing SIR work. The other teachers went to their respective homes. The school peon arrived at 5 PM. He saw the teacher's body hanging. He called the family and the police. The family took him to Bindki CHC, where doctors declared him dead. Family members protested for 4 hours Villagers and family members started shouting slogans against the district administration. Upon receiving information about the incident, Bindki DSP Gaurav Sharma reached the CHC with the Kotwali police force. Officials pacified the family for 4 hours. After this, the family members finally agreed. Police sent the body for post-mortem. After the post-mortem, family members loaded the body into a car and took it to the village. Akhilesh's brother Bhupesh Kumar said- My brother was worried about leave for several weeks for his daughter's wedding. I myself went for leave, but he committed suicide because he didn't get it.

stories.title: UP on high alert as Shia protests erupt over Khamenei:People take to streets; gulf flights cancelled across region
stories.summary: After the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an attack by the United States and Israel, protests have begun in Uttar Pradesh. In Lucknow, thousands from the Shia community came out onto the streets. Women were seen crying and beating their chests. Protesters raised slogans of “Khamenei Zindabad” and “Down with America and Israel”. A woman shouted- Those who have treachery in their blood have killed Khamenei through deception. Khamenei was my lion. If one Khamenei is killed, thousands of Khameneis will rise... Israel and America are deceivers. The All India Shia Personal Law Board has announced three days of mourning. The board’s general secretary, Maulana Yasoob Abbas, said people will put up black flags at their homes and wear black clothes. Religious gatherings will be organised in Khamenei’s name. A large crowd gathered outside Jamia Millia Islamia in southeast Delhi, where people assembled to offer prayers at a nearby mosque following reports of the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in a joint U.S.–Israel strike. The gathering witnessed people expressing grief and solidarity, while groups of students and local community leaders also staged a protest, raising slogans and voicing support for the late Iranian leader.

stories.summary: Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj. He is currently the subject of discussion. There are two reasons for this. First- getting a case of misconduct registered against Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati through two young disciples. Second- he is a history-sheeter in police records. 27 cases are registered against him under serious sections like rape, cow-smuggling, and fraud. But today, we will learn about the second reason for the discussion. The first case against Ashutosh was filed when he was 16 years old. After this, he forged the registrar's signatures to grab land, and a case was filed in that matter. He forged signatures on the file kept in the judge's room and got a non-bailable warrant (NBW) issued. He formed trusts to seize land. He went to bribe the SP in a cow-smuggling case. He seized a house for a school and then faced allegations of raping a widow. Many such cases are registered. The team of Dainik Bhaskar spoke to people associated with these cases. They learned their side of the story. They examined the FIRs and police actions. In today's Sunday Big Story, we will talk about the cases registered against Ashutosh Maharaj First case at the age of 16 Kandhla town is in Shamli district of UP. Raizadgan area is about 20 kilometers away from the district headquarters. This is where Ashutosh Pandey's house is. His father Rajendra Sharma was a conductor in the roadways. Ashutosh's initial name was Ashwini Sharma. After some time, he changed his name to Ashutosh Pandey. Later, he started writing Bhrugvanshi before his name. 5 years ago, Ashutosh changed his name to Brahmachari Maharaj. Now he identifies himself by this name. In 2002, a case was filed against Ashutosh for the first time. Sections 324, 504, 506 were applied. These sections mean - intentionally causing injury, insulting, and threatening. The police administration periodically releases a list of cases registered against Ashutosh Pandey. The list up to 2019 shows a total of 21 cases registered. As of now, a total of 27 cases are registered. Upon gathering information about Ashutosh, it was found that Ashutosh has filed significantly more cases against other people than the cases registered against him. We spoke to people associated with the major cases registered against Ashutosh. Land seized for school, accused of raping a widow The incident dates back to 2010. At that time, Ashutosh Pandey opened a school in Kandhla. For this, he rented the house of a local widow. He paid rent for a few days, but then took possession. He also stopped paying rent. A dispute arose between both parties. It is alleged that in 2012, Ashutosh entered the house of that widow and raped her. The woman filed a case in Kandhla. The victim's sons live in Delhi. They say - the case of raping their mother started in Kairana. He went to the Allahabad High Court to get it dismissed. He also got a stay. We also reached the Allahabad High Court, presented our side. The court removed the stay. Ashutosh was sent to jail. He remained in jail for about 25 days. We are financially weak, we fought the case somehow. The hearing of this case has been completed. Ashutosh will soon be punished. There is not a single person in the area who would call him good. He only commits fraud. Accused of forming a trust to seize 20 bighas of land Our team spoke to many people in Kandhla. One of them was Tarun Agarwal. Tarun's house is near Ashutosh's. He says - The Ramlila Committee in Kandhla has about 20 bighas of land. This land was donated by people of the Vaishya community. We have been maintaining it for 150 years. In 2008, all of us registered the Ramlila Committee. Then we started moving forward accordingly. Ashutosh did not like this. He started conspiring to seize the land. Tarun says- In the year 2008, Ashutosh applied for registration under a different name. At that time, registration work used to happen here in Saharanpur. Ashutosh forged the registrar's signatures in our registration file. He suspended our committee's file. He also took its certified copy. Taking that, he went to the Allahabad High Court. He said that the registrar had suspended the committee. When this file was investigated, the registrar stated that these were not his signatures. Then Ashutosh's lie was caught. In 2012, the registrar had filed a case of fraud. Tarun says - This person has been very advanced in committing fraud. In 2017, he entered a judge's record room in Kairana, forged his signatures, and got the order sheet changed. NBWs were issued against 3 people. Those three people fled to the Allahabad High Court. An investigation revealed that no such order had been given. This order sheet itself was fake. The judge filed a case in 2017. The Shamli Crime Branch was investigating this matter. Got 25 bigha land registered by lying It was learned from the local people of Kandhla that Ashutosh Pandey increased proximity with Krishnapal Gurjar from the neighborhood in 2006. This was because Krishnapal had 25 bigha land. Ashutosh told him that he would get a loan on his land. You won't have to pay much money either. Krishnapal agreed. On the other hand, Ashutosh made arrangements at the Registrar's office. He told Krishnapal that whatever was asked, he just had to say yes. Krishnapal did the same. He got his entire 25 bigha land registered in his name. When this matter came to light, there was an uproar. Krishnapal filed a complaint with the police. The case ran for 5 years, and then the sale deed was returned. It is alleged that at that time, Ashutosh took 8 lakh rupees. He said that so much money was spent in court proceedings. SP caught him in cow-smuggling through a sting operation Upon investigating Ashutosh's crime history, a case from Gonda was found. This case is from 2012, related to cow-smuggling. At that time, Ashutosh met Gonda's SP Navneet Kumar Rana. He said that a truck loaded with animals should be allowed to pass through Gonda's border. He added, "Currently, the police stop it; we will pay money for this." Initially, the SP thought he was crazy, but later, taking it seriously, he called him the next day. SP Navneet Rana informed the DIG and several other officers about this. A CCTV camera was installed in the office. Ashutosh reached the office at 11 AM on January 24. He placed two bundles of 500-rupee notes, totaling 1 lakh rupees, in front of the SP. All of this was recorded on camera. Police personnel present at the spot immediately arrested Ashutosh. Along with Ashutosh, animal traffickers Ibrahim and Firoz were arrested by the police and sent to jail. The trial of the case is ongoing. He stopped the jailer's transfer with a fake letterhead. Ashutosh Pandey was imprisoned in Lucknow jail in 2008. There, he developed a good relationship with the then jailer, Hemant Gupta. Later, he was released on bail, but the relationship continued. The jailer was transferred. Ashutosh committed fraud to stop the transfer. At that time, the BSP government was in power, and the party's national general secretary, Satish Mishra, had influence. Ashutosh created a fake letterhead of Satish Mishra. Then he made a note and personally went to the department to submit it. The jailer's transfer was stopped. When an investigation into this matter began, everyone was stunned, because Satish Mishra had not issued any letter. Police registered a case against Ashutosh at Hazratganj police station in Lucknow. At that time, CO Hazratganj BS Garbyal spoke to Shamli's SP Dehat Rajubabu Singh. Police raided Kandhla, but at that time, the accused Ashutosh was absconding from home. Escaped police custody many times, carried a bounty of 25 thousand Whenever a case was registered against Ashutosh, he would abscond. Police often raided to arrest him. He has been to jail more than 5 times in different cases. In 2019, Ashutosh remained absconding for a long time in a cattle smuggling case. The administration had announced a reward of 25 thousand on Ashutosh. In Shamli, the administration launched Operation Chakravyuh. Under this, people who had rewards on them started being searched for. On October 2, 2019, Ashutosh Pandey was arrested. Considering Ashutosh's long criminal history, Shamli police made him a history-sheeter. His history sheet number was 76A. Ashutosh joined the Brahmin Yuvjan Sabha. He became the national president. He expanded his cadre in different districts. When the Shankaracharya case came to light, Kanpur lawyer Pankaj Dixit came forward. He had also once been associated with the Brahmin Yuvjan Sabha. Pankaj Dixit says - Ashutosh is a big swindler. He used to extort money from people by luring them with promises of jobs in the SP government. In 2018, we filed a case at Swaroop Nagar police station in Kanpur. Due to his habits, the image of the organization was getting tarnished. That's why he was expelled. Pankaj Dixit says - Not only in UP, but cases have been registered against him in different states as well. CM Yogi and former CM Akhilesh Yadav are urged to seriously investigate this matter. Ashutosh is a cunning criminal. To maintain unity and respect in the saint community, the background of such people cannot be ignored. 'Cases filed during SP government lack merit' Recently, Ashutosh Pandey claimed that all the cases registered against him were filed during the SP government. All the cases are political. When we checked the history sheet, it was found that only 5 cases were registered between 2012 and 2017. The remaining cases were either registered during the previous BSP government or after 2017. Ashutosh was declared a wanted criminal during the BJP government. For these reasons, Ashutosh turned against the BJP in the 2022 assembly elections. He openly started campaigning for the SP. He had started a 'Vijay Yatra' (victory march) to make Akhilesh Yadav the Chief Minister. He visited different districts of UP. Speaking to the media, he used to say - 'On March 10, we will perform the 'Pind Daan' (a Hindu ritual for the deceased) of Yogi Adityanath. Brahmins are united and they are going to make Akhilesh Yadav the Chief Minister. The reason for this is that more than 700 Brahmins have been murdered during the Yogi government. More than two and a half thousand Brahmins were sent to jail by filing false cases against them.' Court has stayed the arrest of Shankaracharya Ashutosh Pandey has accused Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand of child sexual abuse. An FIR was registered against Shankaracharya after the court's order. The Allahabad High Court stayed the arrest. Lawyer P.N. Mishra, appearing on behalf of Avimukteshwaranand, presented some points. For instance, the FIR was filed a considerable time after the alleged incident, which raises suspicion. The young students (batuks) who are alleged to have been raped never resided in Shankaracharya's ashram. It was stated that the victim students are regular students at a school in Hardoi and are currently taking exams. How then could they be students of Shankaracharya's ashram? If two students made allegations, then why was only one student presented before the magistrate? On these very points of the lawyer, Justice Jitendra Kumar Sinha stayed the arrest. The hearing will now be in the third week of March. On behalf of the state government, Additional Advocate General Manish Goyal opposed the arrest stay. However, the judge ignored it. Ashutosh has supported different parties at different times. Currently, he identifies himself as the main plaintiff in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi vs Shahi Masjid Idgah case number 4. He also states he is the president of Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Mukti Nirman Trust Mathura. My life is in danger, I will not fight the case now. We spoke to Ashutosh Pandey about all these matters. He says - "Regarding the POCSO case filed against Shankaracharya, I have only provided information in that case. The rule is also that whenever you get information, you can report it. I will not advocate for this case now. I am receiving threats. False cases are being filed against me. I need police protection, but I am not getting it." When asked about the cases filed against him and being a history-sheeter, Ashutosh Pandey says - "Yes, I have been a history-sheeter. If I am wrong, the police should come and arrest me. Why have they left me out until now?"

stories.title: Gujiya selling at ₹31,000 per kg in Kanpur:Gold and silver-leaf sweets dominate market, dry-fruit varieties in demand
stories.summary: With Holi colours in the air, sweetness in the city is set to arrive in a special style this time. Royal gujiyas coated with gold leaf in Kanpur’s sweet market are drawing customers’ attention. This special gujiya, adorned with 24-carat gold leaf, is priced at ₹31,000 per kilogram. It is the most expensive gujiya in the city. A single gold gujiya box costs ₹750. This festive season, the sweet is offering not just taste but a royal experience. Silver gujiya at Rs 2100 per kilo At Pahalwan Ji Namkeen Sweets in Ashok Nagar, more than six flavours of gujiya have been prepared for Holi this year. Shop operators say that besides gold, the royal collection also includes silver-leaf gujiyas priced at ₹2,100 per kg. Shop owner Gaurav Agrawal said these gold and silver-leaf gujiyas were made on special customer demand. They are especially popular for offerings and gifting. Other varieties include fig, saffron and traditional gujiyas. Healthy taste too, demand for fig gujiya Healthy options have also been introduced in the market this time. Special gujiyas made from dry fruits and figs are being sold at ₹1,600 per kg. Saffron gujiyas, syrup-coated traditional gujiyas and mawa special flavours are also attracting buyers. Increased activity in different markets With Holi approaching, gujiya shopping has intensified in the city’s major sweet markets such as Birhana Road, Raina Market, Panki and Lajpat Nagar. Shopkeepers say people this year are increasingly drawn to premium and unique varieties along with traditional flavours.

stories.title: March to bring intense heat wave:Temperature may touch 40 degrees, Uttar Pradesh likely to face stronger summer than last year
stories.summary: Officially, the winter season is considered over from March 1st, and summer begins to knock. This time, with the beginning of March, concerns about the weather have increased. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), this year March could be among the warmest months ever. Maximum and minimum temperatures in northern and northwestern states are expected to be significantly higher than normal. In March 2025, temperatures in many districts reached 35 to 38 degrees. This time, it could be 3-4 degrees higher than that. In such a situation, the big question is, what will the weather be like in March? How much will the heat increase? How much will it affect crops? Read in this report How has the weather been so far? Mahesh Palawat, a weather expert at Noida-based Skymet Weather, explains - Uttar Pradesh experienced less cold this time compared to the last two years. In December-January, the average maximum and minimum temperatures were higher than normal. This time, extreme cold was not observed. Due to La Nia not being active, the cold was not severe. Mohammad Danish, a scientist at the Lucknow Meteorological Center, also states the same. He says - this time, the activity of Western Disturbances remained low in the state during the winter season. Due to this, rainfall was also less than normal during the cold season. How will the weather be in March Weather will change from the first week of March itself BHU meteorologist Manoj Srivastava says - The weather will start changing completely from the first week of March. The summer season will begin. Both day and night temperatures will increase rapidly. By the last week of March, the maximum temperature in many districts of UP can reach 35 to 38 degrees Celsius. IMD's warning about the weather What will be the rain situation in March? According to the Meteorological Department, there is a possibility of average normal rainfall across the country in March 2026. This means that on average, about 30 mm of rain occurs in the country in the month of March. This time too, rainfall is expected to be around this figure. However, the weather will not be the same everywhere. Many parts of the country may experience normal or slightly above normal rainfall. But, some areas in Northeast India and Northwest and East-Central India are likely to receive below normal rainfall. There are also some areas where rainfall is generally very low in March anyway. Therefore, no significant change will be observed there. Temperature remained above normal in February According to scientist Mohammad Danish, the maximum temperature recorded during the hottest day in February 2026 in UP was approximately 29-31 degrees or more. This was significantly higher than the normal February temperature. In Kanpur, on February 23, the mercury reached about 29.6 degrees Celsius. This was reported as the hottest day of the season. This temperature was a record for that time, as such high temperatures are not usually recorded in February. Similarly, on February 24, the maximum temperature in Varanasi was recorded at 31.5 degrees Celsius, which was very high. Meteorological Department expressed concern over crops How will March be for crops? According to BHU agricultural scientist Professor PK Singh, the month of March is considered a crucial time for Rabi crops (wheat, barley, gram, peas). However, the possibility of higher-than-normal temperatures this time has increased farmers' concerns. PK Singh says, "According to the Meteorological Department, temperatures could be 3 to 5 degrees Celsius higher than average. This is likely to have a direct impact on crops. Wheat is currently in the grain formation and ripening stage. If temperatures rise rapidly, the grains may not develop fully. This could lead to a decrease in production." If intense heat occurs prematurely, the crop ripens quickly and the size of the grains remains small. The mustard crop is also in its final stage. Gram and other pulse crops are also likely to be adversely affected by the heat.

stories.title: Burning pyres, ash-covered Naga sadhus play 'Masane ki Holi':Ascetics arrive in Kashi; heavy barricading dampens festival atmosphere
stories.summary: Kashi witnessed a striking and intense scene at the Manikarnika Ghat on Saturday as burning funeral pyres, grieving families, and ash-smeared Naga sadhus came together during the ritual of Masane ki Holi, or Holi of the cremation ground. Naga sadhus and sanyasis celebrated the tradition by applying funeral ashes on their bodies and each other, symbolising detachment from worldly life and the acceptance of death as part of existence. Some sadhus wore garlands made of human skull replicas around their necks, while others danced energetically to the rhythmic beats of the damru. Despite the powerful visuals and deep spiritual significance, this year’s celebration appeared relatively subdued. Authorities had imposed strict barricading at the ghat, and heavy police deployment was in place to regulate crowds and maintain order. Masane ki Holi, a centuries-old tradition associated with Lord Shiva, draws devotees and spectators from across the country, reflecting Kashi’s unique blend of devotion, death, and celebration. Watch the video to witness the rare and intense ritual.

stories.title: 7-Year-old Vaishnavi’s death shocks village:Child with 60% burns dies after week in Lucknow trauma centre; last rites held with abeer-gulal
stories.summary: A wave of grief swept through a village in Barabanki on Saturday after the death of seven-year-old Vaishnavi. Just three days before Holi, her body was brought home, and the entire village broke down in tears. The little girl, with whom the family had planned to celebrate Holi, was instead given a final farewell. Women, children and elderly residents gathered in the narrow village lanes. Every face showed deep sorrow, and many were heard praying that no family should suffer such pain. Vaishnavi had suffered serious burns after falling into boiling water. She was admitted to the Trauma Centre in Lucknow, where she fought for her life for a week. However, she died on Saturday during treatment. In a heartbreaking moment, the grieving family applied abeer and gulal on her face and body before her last rites, as Holi was just days away. As her final journey began, cries and tears filled the air. The last rites were carried out in the presence of police officials. The incident took place in the Kotwadham area of Barabanki district. Now know the full story Sanjay Gupta lives in Kotwadham. On the morning of February 22, his daughter Vaishnavi went to Shivprasad Gupta's shop in the village to buy Maggi. The shopkeeper also makes khoya (mawa) there. Due to this, large pots of boiling water were kept near the shop. Child fell into a pot of boiling water While grabbing the Maggi, Vaishnavi suddenly lost her balance and fell into a pot of boiling water. In the accident, she suffered burns to about 60 percent of her body. Her family immediately rushed her to the hospital. From there, she was referred to the district hospital and then to the Trauma Center in Lucknow. She was admitted to the ICU of the Trauma Center there. Child died after a week of treatment After struggling for life and death in the ICU for a week, her breath stopped on Saturday. Upon reaching the village, the family members, out of tradition and affection, bid farewell to their daughter by applying Holi colors to her. The gulal on the child's face was narrating the story of her unfulfilled joys. Meanwhile, considering the sensitivity of the area, police force and PAC were deployed. The child's last rites were performed in the presence of CO Ramnagar Garima Pant. Mother said - Daughter's room upstairs, no one dares to open it Vaishnavi's mother Geeta Gupta is in a terrible state, crying inconsolably. In a trembling voice, she could only say - Daughter's room is upstairs... no one dares to open it. It's scary. It feels like my life will leave me. That room is still the same today, full of toys. Decorated with colorful clothes and innocent dreams. The mother repeatedly says that this Holi, her daughter will play with lots of colors, she will roam throughout the village and neighborhood. A cheerful, friendly child For the villagers, Vaishnavi was not just a child; she was everyone's darling. Cheerful, friendly to all, she left her mark in every home. Children kept looking for her, and women wept inconsolably in her memory. During the funeral, when people bid her a final farewell by applying gulal, even the onlookers shed tears.
