stories.title: Woman climbs 250-foot mobile tower demanding marriage with lover:Threatens to consume poison if he doesn’t return
stories.summary: A young woman climbed a 250-foot-high mobile tower in Uttar Pradesh’s Maharajganj district on Friday morning, demanding that her lover marry her. She claimed they had been in a relationship for 12 years and accused him of running away from marriage. She also threatened to consume poison in his name if he did not return. The incident took place in Domakati village under Nichlaul police station limits and lasted nearly five hours before police managed to persuade her to come down. Girl throws emotional note from tower While sitting atop the tower, the woman threw down a handwritten note containing the mobile numbers of her lover Farooq and his family members. In the note, she wrote that she loved him deeply and questioned why he was avoiding marriage after being in a relationship for so long. She warned that if he did not return, she would consume poison in his name. She also appealed to him to come back and said she did not feel like living anymore. Police used the phone numbers provided in the note to contact Farooq and his family. Lover summoned from Nepal According to police and family members, Farooq, 22, had gone to Nepal after an argument with the woman, identified as Zora, 18. Nepal is located about 6 kilometres from their village. Zora’s father, Ramzan, a farmer from Piparpati Badhya village, said the couple had been in a relationship for years and their marriage was fixed about a year ago after both families agreed. However, Farooq had recently gone to Bengaluru for work. When he returned three days ago, he refused to marry, which led to a dispute between the two. After the argument, he left for Nepal. Troubled by this, Zora left her house around 5 am on Friday without informing anyone and climbed the mobile tower located about 2 kilometres away. Police and villagers try to convince her Villagers spotted her on the tower and informed police. Officers reached the spot and tried to convince her to come down, but she refused and insisted that Farooq be called to the spot. Police contacted Farooq and asked him to return immediately. He arrived at around 9:30 am and tried to persuade her to come down. However, she refused, saying she feared he might run away again. Police then assured her that they would help resolve the matter and told her she would not be abandoned. After hours of persuasion and assurances, she finally agreed to climb down. Police take both into custody As soon as she came down, police took both Zora and Farooq into custody and brought them to the police station for further inquiry. Nichlaul Station Officer Akhilesh Verma said the woman was safely brought down after counselling and persuasion. “Both have been brought to the police station. Their age and documents are being verified. Further action will be taken based on the family’s complaint,” he said. Police said they are currently examining the legal aspects, including age verification and consent, before deciding on further steps. The situation in the village has now returned to normal

stories.title: 11,000-watt electric shock hits man in UP:Lineman perched on a 25-foot pole to replace transformer, charred to death in fire |VIDEO
stories.summary: A lineman died after suffering an electric shock and catching fire while replacing a transformer in Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh. The incident occurred on a 25-foot-high electricity pole in Lohota village under the Ghorawal police station area. According to eyewitnesses, the lineman had climbed the pole to install a new transformer. During the work, he reportedly received a powerful shock of 11,000 volts. The electric shock caused a short circuit, and flames broke out immediately. Within seconds, the lineman’s body caught fire. His helper present at the spot tried to rescue him, but the lineman had already suffered severe burns. Villagers alleged that the lineman had taken an official shutdown of the power supply before starting the work. However, the electricity supply was allegedly restored while he was still working on the pole, leading to the accident. A video of the incident has also surfaced, showing the lineman engulfed in flames on the pole. Authorities have been informed, and further investigation is underway to determine how the power supply was restored during maintenance work. Heart-wrenching images- Lineman dies after high-voltage shock in Sonbhadra: complete sequence of events Santosh Kumar (40), a resident of Bisahar village, was working as a contract lineman with the electricity department. He lived with his wife Bindu (35) and two sons, Adarsh (15) and Shivam (18). On Thursday evening, Santosh went to Lohota village to install a new transformer. He reached the spot at around 7 pm and began preparations for the work. Shutdown taken before starting work According to his colleagues, Santosh had followed safety procedures. Before climbing the pole, he informed the power house and requested a shutdown to ensure there was no electricity supply during the installation. After receiving confirmation, he climbed the 25-foot-high pole and started mounting the transformer. Power supply suddenly restored While Santosh was working on the pole, the 11,000-volt high-tension supply was suddenly restored without any notice, colleagues alleged. He received a powerful electric shock and got stuck to the pole. A short circuit occurred immediately, and flames broke out. Within moments, Santosh was engulfed in fire while still on the pole. Helper called department, but rescue came too late As soon as the incident happened, helper Matrulal called the electricity department and requested an urgent shutdown. After the supply was cut, he climbed the pole to put out the fire. However, Santosh had already suffered severe burns. With the help of local villagers, he was brought down from the pole and rushed to the district hospital. Doctors referred him to the Trauma Centre in Varanasi due to his critical condition, but Santosh died on the way. The incident has triggered anger among villagers and colleagues, who alleged negligence in restoring the power supply during maintenance work. Authorities have started an investigation into the matter. In this case, the helper who was present with Santosh accused the electricity department of negligence. He said the lineman was working on the line at the time. The department was aware of this, so he questioned on whose orders and why the power supply was restored. Negligence claimed to have cost a life Sonbhadra’s Executive Engineer (XEN) M.B. Thakur said two linemen were working at different locations. Santosh and Matru were together at one site, while Rajesh Sahu was working at another. According to Thakur, after completing his task, Rajesh Sahu restored the power supply. The line became live, leading to the accident. He said the matter is under investigation and further action will be taken based on the findings.

stories.title: Three-day Holi holiday in Uttar Pradesh:4 consecutive days off including Sunday, salaries to be paid before festival
stories.summary: Good news for 1.7 million employees in Uttar Pradesh: the Yogi government has declared a three-day holiday for Holi. Orders were issued on Friday, confirming that March 2, 3, and 4 will be official holidays. Since March 1 is a Sunday, this creates a continuous four-day holiday from Sunday to Wednesday. February 28, i.e., Saturday, has been designated as a working day. All government departments will remain open, and regular work will continue on this day. Salaries must be paid before Holi Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed that all employees, including outsourced, contractual, and sanitation workers, must receive their salaries or honorariums before Holi. He has warned officials that no negligence will be tolerated in this matter. The CM issued these instructions after returning late Thursday night from a foreign tour to Singapore and Japan. Major pay raise for Shiksha Mitras and Instructors Prior to this, the government had announced a significant pay increase for 1.7 lakh Shiksha Mitras and instructors. Shiksha Mitras will now receive ₹18,000 per month, while instructors will get ₹17,000 per month. Previously, Shiksha Mitras received only ₹10,000 and instructors ₹9,000. CM highlights government’s initiatives CM Yogi Adityanath stated in the assembly that the step was taken in the interest of para-teachers and instructors. During the SP government, they received only ₹3,000. His government had increased it to ₹10,000 in 2017, and now, considering inflation, an additional ₹8,000 has been added at once. He also announced 75,000 jobs in the health department, underlining the government’s focus on employee welfare.

stories.title: Allahabad HC stays Shankaracharya’s arrest in sexual abuse case:Order on anticipatory bail reserved; state lawyer says he could influence case
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has stayed the arrest of Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati. Justice Jitendra Kumar Sinha has reserved the order on his anticipatory bail plea, with the next hearing scheduled for the third week of March. The Shankaracharya had filed the anticipatory bail plea on February 24 in connection with a case alleging sexual exploitation of Batuks (young disciples). In court, the state government’s lawyer opposed the bail, while the Shankaracharya’s counsel argued that the case involves a religious leader, not a criminal, and claimed the entire matter is a conspiracy. The government lawyer argued that Shankaracharya is very powerful and could influence the case if granted bail. After the stay on arrest, a celebratory atmosphere was reported at his monastery. Petition filed by Ramabhadracharya’s disciple The case was initiated after Ashutosh Brahmachari, a disciple of Swami Ramabhadracharya, filed a petition under Section 173(4) in the district court. Following the order of Special Judge (Rape POCSO Court) Vinod Kumar Chaurasia, police at Jhunsi Police Station registered an FIR against Swami Avimukteshwaranand over allegations of sexual abuse of Batuks. Lawyer who received bomb threat, accused arrested Meanwhile, police have arrested the accused who threatened to blow up Shankaracharya’s lawyer, Srinath Tripathi, with a bomb. The accused, Ajit Kumar Saroj, was arrested from Rasipur village in the Jansa police station area within about 20 hours. Police said the accused is a law student and also practices in the Varanasi court. During questioning, he admitted that he sent the threatening message to falsely implicate his neighbour. Tripathi received the threat late Wednesday night. The message sent to his mobile phone said, “We will blow up the Varanasi court with a bomb, and you too.” Visitor meets Shankaracharya, calls allegations baseless On Thursday afternoon, a Muslim man met Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand in Varanasi and said the allegations against him were baseless and should not have been made. How the case unfolded The controversy began during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj on January 18, during Mauni Amavasya, when a dispute took place between the Shankaracharya and the administration. On January 24, eight days later, Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj submitted a complaint to the Police Commissioner. The complaint alleged sexual exploitation of children during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025. Alleging police inaction, a petition was filed in the Special POCSO Court on February 8. Two children were produced in court on February 13, and their statements were recorded on February 21. On the same day, the court ordered Jhunsi police to register an FIR. The FIR names Shankaracharya, his disciple Mukundanand, and two to three unidentified persons as accused. Shankaracharya alleges conspiracy, seeks legal relief On February 24, Shankaracharya accused Prayagraj Additional Commissioner Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring against him. He then filed an anticipatory bail petition in the Allahabad High Court. On February 26, the medical report related to the case became public. According to police sources, the report indicates sexual abuse of children. Meanwhile, one of the alleged victims appeared before the media for the first time and claimed he was exploited when he had gone for studies. Responding to the medical report in Varanasi, Shankaracharya questioned the investigation and criticised Ashutosh Maharaj. He alleged that false stories were being spread to create pressure and said he was not afraid of the allegations. Further hearings in the Allahabad High Court and the ongoing police investigation are expected to determine the next course of action in the case.

stories.title: Mayawati to field 100 candidates in next month:Bets on Brahmin-Muslim equation; leads early ticket race
stories.summary: As the much-awaited 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections draw closer, political parties have begun sharpening their strategies. In this race, Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati has stepped up preparations, planning to announce more than 100 candidates within the next month as part of an aggressive early election strategy. So far, BSP has announced four candidates from different regions of Uttar Pradesh — Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, and Western UP. Among them are two Muslim and two Brahmin leaders. This shows that BSP is focusing on a Brahmin-Muslim political combination for the 2027 elections. BSP's strategy is to declare candidates/assembly in-charges for more than 100 seats by March 2026. How effective will BSP's strategy be? How much impact will the Brahmin-Muslim equation have? Read this report… Focus on Brahmin-Muslim-Dalit vote bank In the 2022 Assembly elections, BSP won only one seat but finished second in 18 seats. This time, the party wants to strengthen its position by announcing candidates early and building strong local support. Mayawati has openly appealed to Brahmins and Muslims to support BSP. She says that if Muslims (about 19% of the population) and Dalits (around 20%) vote together, their combined support could reach nearly 39%. If Brahmins (9–11%) also join, the vote share could reach close to 50%, which can help win many seats. Muslims have traditionally supported the Samajwadi Party (SP), while Brahmins are often considered core voters of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). BSP is now trying to attract voters from both parties. Four announced candidates The four candidates announced so far come from different political backgrounds. Some were previously with the Samajwadi Party or the BJP. BSP believes local caste equations — especially Dalit-Muslim and Brahmin-Dalit combinations — can help them win in these constituencies. Target: 100+ candidates by March 2026 According to party sources, BSP aims to finalise candidates in most constituencies by mid-2026. By March, over 100 seats may have declared candidates or assembly in-charges. Several constituencies where BSP finished second in 2022 are also likely to see early candidate announcements. Muslim leaders joining BSP BSP has recently welcomed several Muslim leaders who left SP. The party claims more prominent Muslim faces may join soon. Responsibilities given to senior leaders Mayawati has assigned specific caste outreach responsibilities to senior leaders: Party leaders will soon begin district-level tours and meetings with workers to strengthen the organisation. Overall strategy BSP’s strategy for 2027 is clear: With this plan, Mayawati hopes to revive BSP’s political strength in Uttar Pradesh and challenge both SP and BJP in the next assembly election.

stories.title: Rinku Singh performs his father's last rites:Elder brother Sonu lights the pyre, Virat Kohli offered condolences
stories.summary: India cricketer Rinku Singh suffered a personal loss after his father, Khanchand Singh, passed away on Friday following a long battle with liver cancer at the age of 60. His father had been fighting the disease for some time, and his condition worsened in recent days, leading to his hospitalisation in Greater Noida. He breathed his last this morning at around 4:36 AM. Rinku Singh arrived in Aligarh, leaving the Indian team midway through their T20 World Cup campaign. The Indian cricketer was seen carrying his father's mortal remains on his shoulder before the funeral. 3 pictures from the funeral Rinku's elder brother Sonu lit up the pyre of the his father, according to Hindu traditions. Khanchand Singh was admitted to Yatharth Hospital in Sector Omega One, Greater Noida, after his health suddenly deteriorated. He was diagnosed with stage-four liver cancer and was being treated in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Despite the doctors’ efforts, he could not recover. The tragic news comes at a time when Rinku Singh is part of India’s squad during the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026. The cricketer had briefly left the team’s training camp to be with his father during his critical condition before rejoining the squad. Rinku's father was on a ventilator support for a few days. Rinku’s fiancé and Machhlishahr MP Priya Saroj’s father, Tufani Saroj, spoke to Bhaskar over the phone. He said, "Priya has been with Rinku’s family for several days. We had also gone there at night. While returning, we received the news of his father’s death." What Rinku Singh's father told Bhaskar in his last interview In his last interaction with Bhaskar on the India vs Pakistan match, Rinku's father said he was very happy with his son's performance. "It was a good game. I wasn't feeling well, but now I'm good. I watched the entire match, Rinku is a star now. If he had played more balls, he would scored even more. Father played a key role in Rinku’s journey Rinku Singh has often spoken about the struggles his family faced during his childhood. His father, Khanchand Singh, worked as a gas cylinder delivery man to support the family. In an earlier interview, Rinku shared that he and his four brothers also helped their father by delivering cylinders to homes and hotels on motorcycles. Despite financial hardships, the family always supported Rinku’s cricketing dreams. He and his brothers would even collect money together to buy a cricket ball and play matches in their neighbourhood. Their sacrifices and support played a big role in helping Rinku rise from a humble background to represent India at the highest level. Rinku left team camp to be with his father As soon as Rinku Singh received news about his father’s serious condition, he rushed to the hospital on Tuesday morning, around 10 am. At that time, he was in Chennai with Team India during the T20 World Cup preparations and had to leave the practice session immediately to be with his family. After spending time with his father and family, Rinku returned to Chennai on February 25 and rejoined the Indian team. stories.title: What does Shankaracharya’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ look like?:3-storey building; mirrors on all sides, Mukundanand says there is no swimming pool
stories.summary: Srividya Math in Varanasi has come under national attention after serious allegations were made against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. Jagadguru Rambhadracharya’s disciple, Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj, alleged that the monastery was built like a “Glass Palace” with luxury facilities, including a swimming pool. Following these claims, a case was registered against the Shankaracharya under sexual harassment and POCSO provisions. The allegations led to widespread debate among followers and raised questions about the monastery’s structure and facilities. To verify the claims, a Dainik Bhaskar team visited the Srividya Math and spoke to residents and disciples. Entry restrictions, security and interior layout Security guards were posted outside the monastery. Visitors were allowed entry only after registering their name, address and mobile number. Inside, the main hall had tiled and stone flooring, with carpets placed across the room. The walls were painted in yellow and ochre shades. Several rooms were visible through glass panels installed in doors and partitions. Some followers were seen meditating inside. According to residents, the Shankaracharya was in meditation in a separate private room, where entry is restricted. Disciple Mukundanand said the monastery has multiple floors. The ground floor is used for discourses and meditation. The first floor houses children who study there. The upper floor is reserved for the Shankaracharya. The roof has bathing facilities for children. ‘Mirror palace’ claim and explanation by disciple Mukundanand acknowledged that mirrors were installed across several halls and walls. He said the monastery has many mirrors, which is why people refer to it as a “Mirror Palace”. He denied allegations of a swimming pool inside the building. He said the Ganga flows next to the monastery, and during high water levels, the river reaches the premises. He added that anyone could visit and verify the absence of a swimming pool. A silver throne was also shown inside the monastery, where the Shankaracharya sits in the evening to meet visitors. Author alleges luxury, restricted areas and swimming pool Writer Dr Bhumika Dwivedi, who stayed at the monastery for about two months in 2022 during her research, made several allegations. She claimed the monastery had luxury facilities, including air-conditioned rooms, LED televisions, expensive carpets and marble construction. She alleged that some areas were restricted and controlled by a female associate of the Shankaracharya. According to her, certain rooms and floors were inaccessible to common residents. She also claimed there was a swimming pool on the top floor and an elevator leading to restricted sections. Dwivedi further alleged that children from poor families were made to perform work inside the monastery and that strict control was maintained over access and movement. Shankaracharya and disciple deny allegations Mukundanand rejected the accusations and called them false. He said the monastery follows religious activities and is open to visitors. Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand also denied the claims. He said the allegations were baseless and made out of frustration. He added that any investigation findings would be released by authorities, not individuals. Background of leadership and succession Swami Avimukteshwaranand became head of Jyotishpeeth Badrinath after the death of his guru, Shankaracharya Swami Swaroopanand Saraswati, on September 11, 2022. Swaroopanand Saraswati had served as Shankaracharya of Dwarka and Jyotishpeeth. The controversy surrounding Srividya Math continues, with allegations and counterclaims raising questions that may be resolved through investigation.

stories.title: Lathmar Holi begins in Nandgaon:Women beat Huriyars with sticks; 1 million reach Nand Baba Temple for Gulal celebrations
stories.summary: In Mathura, Lathmar Holi is being played on Thursday at Rangili Chowki in Nandgaon. Decorated friends of Radharani are showering sticks on the 'huriyare' (men who play Holi) who have come from Barsana. The 'huriyare' are blocking their attacks with their shields. During this, a lot of abeer and gulal is also being thrown. Along with this, people are dancing. Around 10 lakh people from India and abroad have reached Nandgaon to witness Lathmar Holi. Lord Krishna spent his childhood in Nandgaon, while Radha ji grew up in Barsana. The distance between these two villages is only 8 KM. It has been a tradition since the Dwapar Yuga that first, Krishna's friends from Nandgaon go to Barsana to play Holi. The next day, the 'huriyare' from Barsana come to Nandgaon to play Lathmar Holi. Before this, Lathmar Holi was played in Barsana on Wednesday (February 25). At that time, the friends of Krishna who had gone from Nandgaon were heavily beaten with sticks by the friends of Barsana. Both were arrested late Thursday night from Tengra turn in the Ramnagar police station area. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) was also present during the operation. Police had announced a reward of ₹25,000 each for information leading to their arrest. Both accused are residents of Ausanganj in the Jaitpura police station area. Police said they were involved in buying and selling codeine cough syrup using fake e-way bills. They also carried out transactions with Shelly Traders, a firm linked to Bhola Jaiswal, father of main accused Shubham Jaiswal. Cases registered in Ramnagar and Kotwali police stations ACP Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh said Manoj Yadav already has a case registered at Kotwali police station for illegal cough syrup trade. Another case against Manoj and Lakshya is registered at Ramnagar police station for illegal supply of cough syrup. Police said the accused traded cough syrup worth lakhs of rupees and had been absconding for several days. Both will be produced in court and sent to jail. Police also said the accused invested money earned from the illegal trade into real estate. Manoj Yadav is linked to a real estate firm named MSS Pharma. Close links with Bhola Jaiswal and Shelly Traders According to police, Manoj Yadav is a close associate of Bhola Jaiswal, who is currently in Sonbhadra jail. Manoj allegedly purchased and supplied large quantities of cough syrup through Shelly Traders. Police said Manoj met Bhola and Shubham Jaiswal through the Saptasagar medicine market. The cough syrup was transported using fake documents. Mastermind Shubham Jaiswal still absconding Police said Bhola Jaiswal has already been arrested in the case, but the main accused, Shubham Jaiswal, is still absconding. He is believed to be abroad. Police said a Red Corner Notice will be issued against him soon. ACP Singh said this is the first time both father and son have been arrested together in the case. Police are continuing interrogation and further investigation. Property worth ₹13.53 crore seized Earlier, on February 24, 2026, Varanasi police seized properties worth ₹13.53 crore belonging to Manoj Yadav. Police also pasted a court notice outside his house and made a public announcement. Police said Manoj Yadav was part of the cough syrup syndicate and had acquired assets through illegal activities. His immovable properties and bank accounts linked to the crime have been frozen as part of legal action.

stories.title: Law student arrested for threatening Shankaracharya’s lawyer:Confesses he sent message to frame neighbour, arrested within 20 hours
stories.summary: Police have arrested a law student for sending a bomb threat to senior advocate and Bar Council of India member Srinath Tripathi, who represents Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. The accused was arrested from Resipur village under Jansa police station area in Varanasi within 20 hours of the complaint. The Varanasi Police Surveillance Cell tracked the mobile number used to send the threat and detained the accused, identified as Ajit Kumar Saroj. He is a law student and also practices under a lawyer at the Varanasi court. Police said he confessed during interrogation that he sent the message to falsely implicate his neighbour. He is being sent to jail under relevant legal provisions. Threat message warned of blowing up court and lawyer The threatening message was sent from an unknown number at 2:23 AM on Thursday. It read: “We will blow up Banaras court with a bomb and you too.” Advocate Srinath Tripathi said he saw the message in the morning while checking his phone and immediately informed senior police officials. He later went to court, where police officers met him and assured him that the accused would be identified soon. Case registered, number traced through surveillance Joint Commissioner of Police Alok Priyadarshini said a case was registered at Bhelupur police station based on Tripathi’s complaint. The SOG-1 team and surveillance unit were assigned to trace the number. Bhelupur police station in-charge Sudhir Kumar Tripathi said the number was traced to Ajit Kumar Saroj, a resident of Resipur village. Police teams reached the location and arrested him. Accused sent threat to frame neighbour, say police During questioning, the accused told police that he sent the threatening message to frame his neighbour due to a personal dispute. Police said further legal action is underway. Police also noted that the Varanasi court has received four bomb threats in the last 14 days. Three of those threats were sent through emails to the district judge. The IT cell is investigating those emails and trying to identify the senders.

stories.title: Hooting at Savarkar tribute event as Aparna Yadav mentions Modi:Protesters object, accuse PM of dividing society through UGC rules
stories.summary: State Women’s Commission Vice President and BJP leader Aparna Yadav faced protests in Lucknow while speaking at a floral tribute programme on Veer Vinayak Damodar Savarkar’s death anniversary. Aparna was addressing the event on nationalism, Hindutva and women empowerment at the Indian Medical Association auditorium. When she mentioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s name during her speech, some people present in the auditorium started hooting and protesting. The protesters alleged that the Prime Minister had divided society through UGC rules. Despite the disruption, Aparna Yadav appealed for calm and continued her speech. Former MP Sadhvi Pragya Thakur attended the programme as the chief guest. The event was organised by Savarkar Vichar Manch, and its members were present in large numbers. Aparna Yadav said – chose BJP, not dynasty politics Aparna Yadav said she joined the Bharatiya Janata Party after leaving the Samajwadi Party to promote nationalism and oppose dynasty politics. She said women’s safety in Uttar Pradesh has improved through the ‘Mission Shakti’ campaign. She also announced that a statue of Veer Savarkar would be installed. Aparna described Savarkar as a great revolutionary and demanded that he be awarded the Bharat Ratna. Now read what Sadhvi Pragya said… ATS tortured for 13 days Sadhvi Pragya Thakur said that standing against injustice is true courage and dharma. Referring to her arrest in the Malegaon blast case, she alleged that the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) illegally detained and tortured her for 13 days. She said she was pressured to name some senior leaders. She added that some people helped bring out the truth and thanked them. A person who divided the country cannot be the ‘Father of the Nation’ Sadhvi Pragya praised Savarkar and said repeated efforts are needed to awaken the nation. She said those who understand the nation and their duty deserve respect like Savarkar. Commenting on Mahatma Gandhi, she said a person responsible for the country’s partition cannot be called the ‘Father of the Nation’. Those with nationalist views were persecuted Sadhvi Pragya said people with nationalist views faced persecution. Referring to her election from Bhopal, she said she considered it an ideological battle and won with public support. She also spoke about the sacrifices made by the families of revolutionaries, especially women in Savarkar’s family. She said despite social pressure and hardships, they remained committed to their cause. She called on the youth to put national interest above everything else.

stories.title: Income Tax raids on BSP MLA Umashankar Singh spark row:Yogi minister protests, officials fear exposure of irregularities
stories.summary: Income Tax Department raids on properties linked to Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) MLA Umashankar Singh have triggered a major political controversy in Uttar Pradesh. Leaders across parties have reacted strongly, with allegations and counter-allegations over the timing and motive of the action. The raids continued for the second consecutive day at several locations connected to Singh, who represents Rasda constituency in Ballia district. Officials have not yet released details of what was recovered during the operation. Minister calls raids politically motivated Dinesh Pratap Singh, minister of horticulture and agricultural export in the Yogi Adityanath government and Umashankar Singh’s relative, termed the raids politically motivated. His daughter is married to Umashankar Singh’s son. He said the action appears driven by political revenge rather than evidence. However, BJP sources said his remarks have drawn objections within the party, and senior leaders have taken note of his statements. Considered influential despite being lone BSP MLA Umashankar Singh is the only BSP MLA in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly and has been considered politically influential for several years. He first became MLA in 2012 after joining BSP in 2011 and was re-elected in 2017 and 2022 from Rasda. Despite being in the opposition, Singh has been seen as having strong influence in departments such as Public Works Department (PWD) and mining. Political observers say his reach in administrative matters is widely discussed in political circles. Questions have also been raised in the past over tenders and mining leases linked to firms associated with him. In one case, a major PWD tender was cancelled after media reports highlighted the issue. Opposition leaders question timing of action BSP chief Mayawati publicly defended Singh. In a post on X, she said Singh has worked with honesty and dedication since joining the party. She added that there have been no complaints from his constituency about illegal property or wrongdoing. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav also criticised the raids and questioned their timing. He suggested that government agencies act selectively and alleged political bias in such actions. Akhilesh also made remarks about the timing of the raids, linking them to political developments and foreign visits by senior leaders. He accused the BJP of using central agencies for political purposes. Close ties with ruling establishment under scrutiny Umashankar Singh has often supported the BJP and NDA in key votes. He voted in favour of NDA candidates in the Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections and supported the BJP in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls. His political and personal connections with leaders in the ruling establishment have drawn attention, especially after the raids. His influence became evident when a bridge built by his firm was inaugurated in Ballia, leading to a dispute with Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh. There have also been allegations that officers close to him received key postings in certain districts, though no official confirmation has been made. Political implications ahead of elections Political analysts believe the raids could have wider political implications. As the only BSP MLA in the Assembly, Umashankar Singh plays a key role in maintaining the party’s presence in the House. Some experts believe the raids may be aimed at examining financial links and gathering evidence related to contracts and political funding. Others say central agencies do not conduct such operations without evidence. The Income Tax Department has not issued an official statement on the findings so far. The raids and the political reactions have intensified debate over the use of investigative agencies in politically sensitive cases in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.summary: The Iran war has quickly become attritional, with Iranian drone attacks depleting US and partner weapon stockpiles. While Patriot missiles are effective, their high cost against cheap drones highlights a critical resource challenge. The conflict's outcome may hinge on which side exhausts its munitions first.

stories.title: Top Iran official vows attacks on tankers using Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: An Iranian military official threatened to "set on fire" ships in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil transit route. This warning follows US and Israeli strikes, leading most shipping companies to halt passage through the strait. The reduced traffic raises concerns about oil supply disruptions and potential price hikes for consumers.

stories.title: Iran's strategy: Expand war, increase cost, outlast Donald Trump
stories.summary: Iran's survival hinges on escalating regional conflict, aiming to raise the cost for the US through attacks on oil infrastructure and shipping. This strategy seeks to pressure President Trump into withdrawing by disrupting global economies and exhausting enemy defenses. Analysts believe Iran is prepared for a prolonged struggle, testing international will.

stories.title: US, Israel attacks Iran: AIMPLB urges UN to take steps for ceasefire
stories.summary: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board has strongly condemned the US-Israel's actions against Iran, calling for immediate international intervention to secure a ceasefire. The board expressed sorrow over the reported martyrdom of Iran's supreme leader, Ayatollah Khamenei, and highlighted that targeting leadership and advocating regime change violates international law.

stories.title: Under pressure, Karnataka to revise internal quota of SC communities
stories.summary: Karnataka's Congress government is reconsidering its decision to fill 56,432 government posts without internal reservation for Scheduled Castes. Following pressure from SC communities and ministers, the cabinet will discuss introducing pro-rata internal reservation within the existing 15% SC quota.

stories.title: Nitish's son Nishant set for political launch ahead of Rajya Sabha election
stories.summary: Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's son, Nishant Kumar, is reportedly set to enter politics, marking a shift from his father's stance against dynastic succession. This move comes amid growing internal party pressure and concerns about leadership transition, with Nishant seen as a potential link to traditional JDU supporters.

stories.summary: Move To Cement Party President's Presence In National Politics

stories.title: Adin Ross sister Madeline Ross dies at 36 in Broward County Florida, cause of death pending
stories.summary: Madeline Ross, sister of streamer Adin Ross, died on January 15 in Broward County, Florida, at age 36. The Broward County Medical Examiner confirmed the news to TMZ. stories.title: “Connecting dots” Journalist defends Candace Owens amid Bride of Charlie controversy, claims Charlie Kirk mystery will be solved

stories.title: Data centres new target in Iran conflict; 3 Amazon units hit by drones in UAE, Bahrain

stories.title: Parliament must debate 'dissonance' in foreign policy: Congress MP Sonia Gandhi

stories.title: Was the US attack on Iran predicted just days before? Ex-CIA officer John Kiriakou's shocking warning
stories.summary: Following Operation Epic Fury, the United States and Israel launched sweeping strikes on Iran’s missile and nuclear infrastructure, an assault that killed Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, and triggered widespread regional retaliation. stories.title: PM Modi calls for export push, puts biopharma at centre stage

stories.title: Iran crisis: PM Modi talks to leaders of Qatar, Oman, Kuwait

stories.title: From CAA criticism to Kashmir remark: History that frames India’s silence over Khamenei’s demise

stories.title: From Khamenei's compound to nuclear complex: Satellite images show aftermath of Iranian sites after US-Israel strikes
stories.summary: High-resolution satellite images reveal extensive destruction across Iran following US-Israeli strikes on nuclear, military, and leadership sites. stories.title: YMCA vs Hijab: How Iranian women are hitting back at moral policing on social media after Khamenei death
stories.summary: One widely circulated video showed a young Iranian American woman dancing provocatively to what online observers dubbed the “Trump dance,” a meme adaptation of YMCA choreography synonymous with campaign rallies. stories.summary: Dubai, once a symbol of Middle Eastern stability, now faces unprecedented threats after Iranian missile and drone strikes targeted its airport and iconic landmarks. US-Israel strikes in Iran: Indian national killed in attack on oil tanker off Oman coast
stories.summary: An Indian national has died after an oil tanker, the MKD VYOM, was attacked by an unmanned boat off the coast of Oman. The strike caused a fire and explosion in the vessel's engine room. This incident occurs amid heightened tensions and ongoing retaliation campaigns in the Gulf region.

stories.title: US-Iran war: Kuwait 'mistakenly' shoots down three American F-15s in friendly fire incident
stories.summary: Three US F-15E fighter jets crashed in Kuwait early Monday due to a friendly fire incident, according to US central command. All six crew members ejected safely and are in stable condition. The incident occurred amidst escalating regional tensions and Iranian retaliatory strikes, with Kuwait also intercepting hostile drones. The cause is under investigation.

stories.title: US, Israel wipe out key Iranian leaders in attack blitz; how it may be a tactical blunder
stories.summary: The targeted killing of Iran's Supreme Leader has escalated into a regionwide conflict, with the US and Israel facing a complex reality as Iran signals continuity. This strategic gamble risks a prolonged, multi-actor war, potentially backfiring by strengthening the regime's internal cohesion and creating widespread instability.

stories.title: US-Iran war: 'Several' American warplanes crash in Kuwait, crew survive
stories.summary: Multiple US military aircraft crashed in Kuwait early Monday, with all crew members surviving and in stable condition. The incidents occurred as Kuwait reported intercepting hostile drones, with Iran's state media claiming responsibility for hitting a US plane that crashed in the region. Smoke was also observed near the US embassy compound.

stories.title: “He was going to get killed”: Pastor speaks out after Candace Owens suggests Charlie Kirk feared assassination
stories.summary: Candace Owens stirred controversy by sharing an anonymous email claiming Charlie Kirk told a pastor he feared being killed before his death. Trinity Church pastor Mark Driscoll strongly denied the allegation, calling it false and criticizing Owens’ claims. Kirk was fatally shot during a Utah campus event. The dispute highlights growing misinformation concerns and competing narratives surrounding the tragic incident.

stories.title: Israel-Iran conflict: What is India’s position amid rising Middle East tensions?
stories.summary: India advocates for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve escalating West Asian conflicts, expressing grave concern over recent US-Israeli strikes on Iran. Prime Minister Modi emphasized civilian safety and urged maximum restraint from all parties. New Delhi is actively monitoring the situation and ensuring the well-being of Indian nationals in the region.

stories.title: Total lunar eclipse on March 3, 2026 will be the last one visible until 2029
'90cr given via DBT to 30,000 girls in first phase of ladli scheme': Delhi CM Rekha Gupta
stories.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Monday launched key women-centric initiatives at the Sashakt Nari, Samriddh Delhi programme, including the free LPG cylinder scheme for ration card holders and the Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana.

stories.title: Iran's Natanz nuclear site hit: Tehran vows to rebuild facility; IAEA flags radiation risk
stories.summary: Iran's Natanz nuclear facility was reportedly targeted in recent US and Israeli military operations, according to Tehran's UN envoy. President Pezeshkian vowed to rebuild, asserting Iran's nuclear program is for civilian use, not weapons. IAEA chief Grossi expressed grave concern over potential radiological releases, urging restraint amid escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Typo or insult? Arab man faces Sharjah Court over WhatsApp spelling error
stories.summary: A Sharjah court heard a case where a man faces electronic insult charges due to a spelling mistake in a WhatsApp message. The defendant claims the word was a typo, not an intentional insult, during an exchange initiated on a vehicle sales website. The court has adjourned the session to allow for an amicable settlement between the parties.

stories.title: ‘Burn in hell’: Escaped Iranian-Australian news host reacts to Khamenei’s death — video
stories.summary: Iranian-Australian broadcaster Rita Panahi expressed jubilation on air following reports of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's death in US-Israeli strikes, declaring "the dictator is dead, and Iran is on the verge of being liberated." She praised President Trump's "courage" for the "Operation Epic Fury" strikes, which she believes could free millions from "brutal Islamist rule."

stories.title: Emirates extends suspension of Dubai flights as Middle East Airspace shuts down
stories.summary: Emirates has extended its flight suspension to and from Dubai until March 3, 2026, due to ongoing regional airspace closures. Escalating US-Israel-Iran tensions have led multiple countries to shut their airspace, impacting over 1,800 flights and major hubs like Dubai International Airport. Operations will resume once safety is confirmed by authorities.

stories.title: US-Israel attack Iran: Saudi capital Riyadh becomes evacuation hub for wealthy individuals
stories.summary: Riyadh has become a crucial evacuation hub for wealthy individuals and executives as missile and drone attacks disrupt previously secure Gulf cities. With limited alternatives, the Saudi capital's open airspace and operating airport offer the most viable departure point for those seeking to leave the region.

stories.title: 'Matter of grave concern': PM Modi calls for dialogue and diplomacy as Middle East tensions soar
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi voiced deep concern over the escalating Middle East situation. This follows significant military action by the United States and Israel against Iran. The strikes led to the death of Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. India will work with regional nations to ensure the safety of its citizens.

stories.title: UAE gold prices jump over Dh10 as US–Iran tensions escalate in Middle East
stories.summary: Gold prices in the UAE surged dramatically on March 2, 2026, by over Dh10 per gram, mirroring global anxieties over escalating Middle East conflicts. This safe-haven rally, fueled by geopolitical tensions and persistent inflation, saw 24K gold reach Dh646.45 per gram. Analysts predict continued strength for gold as a hedge against global uncertainty.

stories.title: Iran conflict disrupts air travel; Emirates, Etihad, Air India, IndiGo issue advisories
stories.summary: Escalating Middle East tensions following US-Israel strikes on Iran and Tehran's retaliation have led to widespread flight cancellations and airspace closures across several Gulf nations. Major hubs like Dubai and Doha are affected, with thousands of passengers stranded as airlines divert or suspend services, impacting travel between continents

stories.title: Shooting in US: One killed during opening of Nipsey Hussle's Marathon Burger
stories.summary: A deadly shooting occurred during the grand opening of Marathon Burger, a restaurant co-founded by the late rapper Nipsey Hussle. The incident, reported on Pine Avenue, resulted in one fatality and two individuals sustaining injuries. Police are actively investigating the shooting, with no suspect or motive yet announced.

stories.title: US F-15 down in Kuwait? Iran shares video showing fighter jet engulfed in flames, pilots ejecting
stories.summary: US F-15 Fighter Jet Crash: An American F-15 fighter jet crashed in Kuwait amid escalating Middle East tensions following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. While Iran's state media claimed the jet was shot down, the exact cause remains unconfirmed. Both crew members reportedly survived and were handed over to Kuwaiti authorities

stories.title: MHA alerts states as Middle East tensions soar; internet curbs, security tightened in Kashmir
stories.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs has alerted states to potential tensions due to the Iran conflict, urging vigilance against inflammatory religious gatherings and radical preachers. Authorities are monitoring individuals and groups to prevent unrest, with precautionary measures already implemented in Jammu and Kashmir following protests over the killing of Iran's supreme leader.

stories.title: Interior Ministry Warning: UAE urges vigilance after scam calls spike; legal action planned
stories.summary: UAE residents are cautioned about a rise in fraudulent calls in which impersonators pretend to be officials to steal personal data. The Interior Ministry has denied any link to suspicious numbers such as 70614213 and urges the public not to share sensitive information.

stories.title: Kuwait: Interior Ministry announces temporary ban on fishing boats and outdoor gatherings amid Iran-Israel conflict
Flu shot to change this year as new H3N2 strain spreads fast
stories.summary: India is updating its seasonal flu vaccine for the 2026-27 season to combat a rapidly spreading new A(H3N2) variant. The World Health Organization's recommendations highlight the need for this change due to the strain's increased transmissibility. Experts urge early vaccination, especially for vulnerable groups, to prevent severe illness and hospitalizations.

stories.title: Satellite images show impact of Iran missile and drone attacks on Dubai
stories.summary: Following the killing of its Supreme Leader, Iran launched retaliatory strikes across the Middle East, targeting American military bases and Israel. Dubai, a symbol of modern opulence, was also hit, with iconic landmarks like the Burj Al Arab and vital infrastructure such as Dubai International Airport sustaining damage amidst widespread attacks.

stories.title: ‘Gave us free food and hotel vouchers’: Stranded Indian traveller praises UAE support after airspace shutdown
'Your wife is Indian': US rep Brandon Gill faces backlash over anti-immigration post
Taliban strike multiple military bases in Pakistan; strategic Nur Khan Airbase in Rawalpindi hit
stories.summary: Afghanistan's Air Force launched drone strikes on key Pakistani military bases, including Nur Khan Airbase and Quetta's 12th Corps HQ. This retaliatory action follows Pakistan's recent aerial incursions into Afghan territory. Both nations have engaged in escalating tit-for-tat clashes, with Pakistan claiming significant Taliban fighter casualties and Afghanistan asserting the downing of a Pakistani jet.

stories.title: Safe-haven image cracks as Iran drones target US Gulf allies; Dubai hotel, airport hit
All expenses paid: UAE covers accommodation, meals, flights for 20000+ stranded travellers in emirates amid Iran–US–Israel war
stories.summary: The UAE is stepping in to help thousands of travellers stranded by flight cancellations. The government will cover all accommodation and meal costs for passengers affected by the ongoing aviation crisis. Major UAE airports like Dubai and Abu Dhabi are facilitating rebooking and providing essential support. This move ensures passenger welfare during a period of significant travel disruption.

stories.title: Khamenei sought to turn Iran into a regional powerhouse
Iran war: Khamenei had planned for transition of power
UAE intercepts drone, debris injures civilians as it hits Etihad Towers in Abu Dhabi amid Iran–US–Israel conflict
stories.summary: Drone debris from intercepted threats struck Abu Dhabi's Etihad Towers, injuring a woman and child. This incident highlights the spillover of the Iran-US-Israel conflict into the UAE, with similar debris falling in Dubai. Authorities confirm successful interceptions but acknowledge collateral damage, urging reliance on official updates amid heightened regional tensions.

stories.title: IAF starts process to acquire 4-6 long-range biz jets for military leadership, ministers
Iranian state media claims US fighter jet downed in Kuwait; explosions in Bahrain, Dubai, Doha
Middle East tensions surge: Saudi Arabia summons Iran envoy in escalating Gulf crisis amid US-Israel attacks
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has summoned Iran's ambassador. This action follows Iranian attacks on Saudi territory and neighbouring Gulf states. The move escalates tensions linked to the ongoing US-Israel conflict with Iran. Other Gulf nations like Kuwait and Qatar have also protested Iranian actions. Saudi Arabia vows to defend its sovereignty and security.

stories.title: 4,000-year-old 36 swords seized at a US port in Philadelphia in a bizarre smuggling case
stories.summary: US Customs and Border Protection seized 36 Bronze Age short swords and 50 arrowheads, nearly 4,000 years old, at the Port of Philadelphia. The ancient Iranian artifacts were misdeclared as 'metal decorations' and routed through multiple countries, likely destined for the illicit antiquities market. Archaeologists confirmed their authenticity and cultural heritage value.

stories.title: GCC's largest container port Jebel Ali hit amid Iran-US-Israel war? DP World responds as Epstein scandal haunts its Dubai operations
stories.summary: Dubai's Jebel Ali Port, a global trade linchpin, has temporarily ceased operations following a fire caused by aerial debris amidst escalating US-Israel conflict with Iran. This precautionary shutdown highlights the widening regional instability, impacting vital supply chains and underscoring the vulnerability of critical infrastructure. The incident adds to DP World's recent corporate scrutiny after Epstein Files controversy.

stories.title: GCC's largest container port Jebel Ali hit amid Iran-US-Israel war? DP World responds as Epstein scandal haunts its Dubai operations
stories.summary: Jebel Ali is the largest port in the Middle East and one of the world’s busiest container terminals. It serves as a major transshipment and re-export hub linking Asia, Europe and Africa.

stories.title: Counting pills, fearing blasts: Indians stranded in West Asia
stories.summary: Thousands of Indians are stranded across West Asia as US-Israel strikes on Iran triggered retaliatory actions, leading to widespread airspace closures. Dubai, a major transit hub, is severely affected, with numerous flights cancelled. Tourists, expatriates, and families are facing financial hardship and uncertainty, with some seeking shelter with locals.

stories.title: Priyanka Gandhi: Iran leader's killing 'despicable'
Oil tanker carrying 15 Indian nationals, 5 Iranians attacked near Oman coast, 4 crew injured
Iran war: Air travel crippled as almost 2,000 flights cancelled
Refunds, free hotels, rebooking, food provisions for tourists stuck in UAE
stories.summary: Air travel in the Middle East is severely disrupted as the US-Israel war on Iran leads to extensive flight cancellations and airspace closures. Major UAE carriers have suspended operations, stranding thousands of tourists. Authorities are providing support, including accommodation and meals, while advising passengers to check flight statuses and know their rights.

stories.title: US–Israel war on Iran: Dos and don’ts for UAE residents amid high alert
stories.summary: As the US and Israel's military campaign against Iran escalates, the UAE implements broad public safety measures. Residents are urged to comply with official instructions, seek shelter during alerts, and avoid spreading unverified information, which carries legal penalties. Educational institutions have shifted to distance learning, and travel disruptions persist due to airspace closures.

stories.title: PM Modi reviews West Asia situation, evacuation after attacks subside
UAE stock markets close, trading halted by Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange and the Dubai Financial Market for two days amid Iran–US–Israel war fallout
stories.summary: The UAE has shut its Dubai and Abu Dhabi stock markets for two days, March 2-3, 2026, due to escalating Iran-US-Israel conflict fallout. This unprecedented move follows Iranian retaliatory strikes, disrupting regional business and investor confidence. Other Gulf markets saw sharp declines, with oil prices surging amid fears of supply disruptions.

stories.title: 'Bombing a country won’t make the Epstein files go away,' Rep. Thomas Massie warns after US-Israel launch strike on Iran
stories.summary: Representative Thomas Massie criticizes President Trump's military actions in Iran, suggesting they are intended to distract from the release of Jeffrey Epstein documents. Massie, who co-sponsored legislation to declassify Epstein files, argues that such foreign policy maneuvers do not negate the need for transparency.

stories.title: 'Conveyed India's concerns over recent developments': PM Modi speaks to Israel's Netanyahu
Is Sahara Desert dust secretly feeding the Amazon? The science behind a 10,000-mile journey
stories.summary: In 2015, NASA-backed research led by Hongbin Yu revealed that millions of tons of Saharan dust cross the Atlantic each year, delivering vital phosphorus to the nutrient-poor Amazon rainforest. Satellite data showed this atmospheric link may replenish nutrients lost to rainfall, highlighting a vast intercontinental exchange that underscores how climate and ecosystems remain deeply interconnected.

stories.title: Texas bar shooting: Suspect wore ‘Property of Allah’ hoodie, undershirt referring to Iran and had a Quran in his car — what we know about Ndiaga Diagne
stories.summary: An ex-New York resident, identified as Ndiaga Diagne, is suspected of carrying out a deadly shooting at a Texas bar. Law enforcement sources suggest a possible motive of vengeance related to US actions in Iran, citing a "Property of Allah" hoodie and an Iranian flag symbol.

stories.title: UAE airspace chaos: Sharjah Airport issues passenger advisory amid US-Israel war on Iran, flight disruptions
stories.summary: Sharjah International Airport is experiencing significant flight disruptions, including cancellations and delays, due to temporary UAE airspace closures. These measures are a direct response to escalating US-Israel military actions against Iran and subsequent regional security concerns. Passengers are strongly advised to verify flight statuses with airlines before traveling to avoid unnecessary inconvenience.

stories.title: 'India stands in solidarity': PM Modi speaks to UAE prez, condemns attacks by Iran
LoC drone intrusions force closure of Kashmir schools till March 3
'They want to talk, and I agreed': Trump claims Iran seeking dialogue
stories.summary: President Trump stated in an interview that Iran's new leadership wants to talk, and he has agreed to discussions. He expressed confidence in an upcoming uprising, noting celebrations among Iranians and expatriates. Trump also indicated he would assess support for any potential uprising at the time it occurs.

stories.title: PMO seeks third-party audits for road, rail projects; highway ministry asked to study GQ-era construction
Ban, regulate or reform? Social media & under-15s – The India question
stories.summary: India is debating a ban on social media for children under 15. Global trends show stricter digital safety laws for minors. Experts cite risks like addiction and bullying. The country must balance protection with access. Solutions may involve design reform and digital literacy. This decision impacts millions of young users.

stories.title: America First, Diplomacy Last: The Peace President who went to war
stories.summary: Donald Trump, once a critic of 'endless wars,' now presides over a presidency marked by muscular interventions. His second term features forceful actions in Venezuela and Iran, alongside territorial ambitions towards Greenland. This shift from a 'peace president' to one employing high-stakes brinkmanship redefines 'America First' as forceful global reshaping, aiming for dominance rather than negotiated equilibrium.

stories.title: Almost all US Military bases hit by Iran: Is America unable to safeguard its assets Middle-East?
stories.summary: Following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, Tehran launched a wide-ranging retaliatory campaign targeting US and Israeli military assets across the Middle East. Multiple Gulf nations reported missile and drone attacks, with US Central Command confirming three American service members killed. The scale of the strikes raises questions about regional air defence capabilities and potential escalation.

stories.title: ‘Patriots, keep protesting’: Iranian prayer app with five million users hacked by Israel, says report
stories.summary: Iran's popular prayer app, BadeSaba Calendar, broadcasted anti-regime messages urging security forces to defect amid heightened unrest and foreign strikes. Screenshots circulated before a near-total internet blackout. While Israel hasn't confirmed, reports suggest this is part of its strategy to shape behavior through precise, psychologically impactful cyber operations, turning trusted tools into vulnerabilities.

stories.title: 3 people, including gunman, killed; 14 injured in Texas bar shooting
stories.summary: A shooting at Buford's bar in Texas resulted in at least three deaths, including the alleged gunman, and 14 injuries. Police responded rapidly to the scene, engaging and killing the suspect. The swift actions of emergency services are credited with saving lives amidst the chaos.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu polls: PM Modi targets DMK over corruption, Katchatheevu; calls ‘no fear’ remark a badge of honour
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi launched a scathing attack on Tamil Nadu's DMK, accusing leaders of prioritizing scams over public welfare and failing to protect state interests. Addressing a rally, he asserted NDA's victory in the upcoming elections, highlighting issues like Katchatheevu, Jallikattu, and women's safety, while also inaugurating development projects.

stories.title: ‘48 Iranian leaders gone’: Trump claims major success as conflict with Iran escalates
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that 48 Iranian leaders have been killed in US-Israeli strikes, describing the operation as ahead of schedule. This follows joint strikes that killed Iran's supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, prompting Iranian counterattacks across the region. The US reported three service members killed and five wounded amid escalating hostilities.

stories.title: Former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad killed in Israeli airstrikes on Tehran: Report
stories.summary: Former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad has reportedly been killed in Israeli airstrikes within Iran. Reports suggest he was under house arrest at the time of the targeted strike on his residence. Ahmadinejad, known for his hardline stance and controversial remarks, served as Iran's president from 2005 to 2013, often drawing international criticism for his rhetoric.

stories.title: 'Situation is fluid': US confirms 3 soldiers killed, several injured in 'Operation Epic Fury' against Iran
stories.summary: Three U.S. service members were killed and five seriously wounded during 'Operation Epic Fury,' a U.S.-led offensive targeting Iran's leadership. The operation, which also involved Israeli forces, aimed for a 'decapitation strike' and resulted in significant casualties, including at a girls' school.

stories.title: Donald Trump hosts fundraiser at Mar-a-Lago as Middle East lights up with Iranian missiles targeting US and its allies
stories.summary: While Iran vowed retaliation for airstrikes that reportedly killed its Supreme Leader, President Trump attended a Mar-a-Lago fundraiser. He mingled with donors and danced to music as US military prepared joint strikes on Iran. Trump later announced the war's commencement on Truth Social.

stories.title: 'US crossed dangerous red line': Iran says has no option but to respond after Khamenei killing
stories.summary: Iran has issued a stark warning to the United States, declaring the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei a "dangerous red line" that necessitates retaliation. Following joint US-Israeli strikes, Iran launched a significant wave of attacks across the Middle East, targeting countries hosting US bases.

stories.title: 'Missiles didn't come close': US rubbishes Iran's 'struck' USS Abraham Lincoln claim
Rosanna Pansino questions MrBeast’s YouTube views after Beast Industries CEO claims 1.45 billion reach
stories.summary: Rosanna Pansino questioned whether MrBeast’s reported 1.45 billion viewers included paid promotions after a claim by Beast Industries CEO Jeff Housenbold. She said she was citing public ad data, not making an accusation. Online reactions were divided. Neither MrBeast nor his company has responded, while his recent “negative money” comment also drew attention.

stories.title: After Nancy Guthrie’s kidnapping, Arizona residents rush to build 'safe rooms' with heavy-duty doors
stories.summary: Following Nancy Guthrie's month-long disappearance after a home kidnapping, Arizona residents are urgently installing panic rooms. Businesses specializing in secure "safe rooms" report a significant surge in demand, with families seeking protection against home invasions. These reinforced, hidden rooms offer a sanctuary against potential threats.

stories.title: ‘Demon of our times eliminated’: Iran’s exiled prince Raza Pahlavi on Khamenei's death
stories.summary: Exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi declared the Islamic Republic nearing its end following supreme leader Khamenei's reported death in US-Israeli strikes. He warned against appointing a successor, deeming it illegitimate and urging officials to surrender power to the people. Pahlavi called for a "Lion and Sun Revolution" and appealed to armed forces to join the public's demand for regime collapse.

stories.title: Khamenei dead, Iranians flood streets: Trump wants protesters to ‘take over,' but can they?
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei is dead, triggering celebrations and mourning across the nation. The US and Israel see this as an opportunity for regime change, while Iran's leadership signals escalation with retaliatory strikes. The country faces a critical juncture as popular anger clashes with the security apparatus's control.

stories.title: President Murmu to launch free pink mobility card for women in Delhi
‘Very disturbing’: Thousands of Indians stuck in Iran and Gulf as Middle East conflict escalates
Famous photo of Bill Clinton in hot tub with woman taken during 2002 Asia trip with Epstein and Maxwell: Report
stories.summary: A shocking 2002 photo of Bill Clinton in a Brunei hotel hot tub with an unidentified woman has surfaced, linked to a trip with Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. Clinton, who travelled on Epstein's private jet, denied wrongdoing and knowing the woman during a deposition. The opulent suite and the company kept raise serious questions.

stories.title: Solo act or silent understanding? Congress and the Left in Bengal

Evening news wrap: IDF reveals Khamenei’s location at time of strike; Alireza Arafi named Iran’s interim supreme leader & more
‘Cynical violation of law’: Russia, China condemn killing of Khamenei in US-Israel strikes
stories.summary: The assassination of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes has ignited sharp criticism from Russia and China, who decry the act as a violation of international law and sovereignty. Both nations urge an immediate halt to military operations, highlighting escalating regional instability and a widening geopolitical divide.

stories.title: MrBeast wins hearts as he shares heartfelt perspective on why fan encounters truly matter
stories.summary: MrBeast shared why he values taking photos with fans, saying the moment may be their only chance to meet someone famous. He explained that while creators experience thousands of interactions, fans remember these encounters for years. Viewing each meeting as “1 of 1” helps him stay present and go above and beyond, strengthening the emotional connection between creator and audience.

stories.title: Drake and Kai Cenat feud: Streamer demands rapper “drop the album” after Vivet joke
stories.summary: Kai Cenat sparked online buzz after telling Drake to “drop the album” following the rapper’s joke about being a “Vivet designer” for Cenat’s new fashion brand. The playful exchange quickly turned into renewed pressure from fans awaiting Drake’s rumored ICEMAN project. Meanwhile, Cenat continues focusing on self-growth and creativity as he builds his Vivet label and expands his influence beyond streaming.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia arrests 19,077 residency, border and labour law violators in one week
Middle East crisis: Oil tanker hit near Oman in Strait of Hormuz; 15 Indians evacuated
stories.summary: An oil tanker, the Skylight, was attacked off Oman's coast, injuring four crew members and prompting an evacuation. This incident follows Iran's warning to close the vital Strait of Hormuz, a key global oil route. Shipping giants are suspending transit, and insurers are withdrawing cover, raising fears of severe global energy market disruption amid escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: 'Crumbling empire’: What Khamenei said about US in his last public speech
“Charlie just go for it…”: Candace Owens revealed she encouraged Charlie Kirk to pursue Erika despite early hesitation
stories.summary: A resurfaced clip of Candace Owens recounting how she encouraged Charlie Kirk to pursue Erika has ignited viral speculation online. While the anecdote describes a warm first meeting and supportive advice, social media narratives quickly spiraled into conspiracy claims. The episode highlights how context-free clips can fuel misinformation and demonstrates the speed at which viral outrage can distort straightforward personal stories.

stories.title: US-Israel stikes on Iran: Tehran fired missiles towards UK bases in Cyprus, says defence secretary
stories.summary: Iran fired two missiles towards Cyprus, where the UK has military bases, with Defence Secretary John Healey stating the attacks showed indiscriminate retaliation. He confirmed UK military personnel were near missile strikes in Bahrain, emphasizing the need for Iran to halt its actions and weapons programs.

stories.title: Who is Ayatollah Alireza Arafi? Iran’s interim Supreme Leader after Khamenei’s death
stories.summary: Iran has appointed Ayatollah Alireza Arafi as interim supreme leader following the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Arafi, a seasoned cleric with deep ties to the establishment, faces the immense task of navigating regional tensions and internal instability. His elevation signifies a crucial leadership transition, testing Iran's political resilience as it seeks a permanent successor.

stories.title: 'Help has now arrived': Netanyahu sends message to Iran citizens, warns of more strikes against 'terrorist regime'
stories.summary: In the wake of Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Khamenei's death in a joint US-Israel strike, Netanyahu warned to hit thousands of targets, framing the moment as a historic window for Iranians to challenge the regime. Reports describe coordinated operations targeting critical Iranian military hubs and infrastructure, aiming to dismantle the government and remove threats.

stories.title: World Clap Day: ‘Imagine the entire planet clapping together at once,’ one-man's vision for 16 August 2026
stories.summary: Founded in London in December 2025 by Andrea Bechis, World Clap Day plans a synchronized global clap on 16 August 2026 at 10:00 PM EDT. Framed as a non-political celebration of humanity, the initiative has grown rapidly online, drawing hundreds of thousands of supporters and positioning a one-second gesture as an annual worldwide moment of unity.

stories.title: Iran strikes Gulf states, even mediator Oman – why its strategy could backfire
stories.summary: Iran has escalated its conflict by targeting Gulf Arab states, including Oman and the UAE, in a bid to pressure the US. Analysts suggest this move risks pushing regional powers closer to Washington, despite Iran's aim to compel de-escalation. The strikes, hitting civilian areas and ports, signal a broader regional involvement, potentially forcing Gulf nations to reconsider their stance.

stories.title: ‘Legitimate duty and right’: Iran's Prez vows revenge after Khamenei's assassination
stories.summary: Iran's President vows revenge for Supreme Leader Khamenei's killing in US-Israeli strikes, calling it a 'declaration of war.' The assassination creates a leadership vacuum and sparks regional unrest, with Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatening severe retaliation. Amidst a near-total internet blackout, Tehran views this as a pivotal moment in the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: 'He was in central leadership compound in heart of Tehran': IDF issues statement on Khamenei's death
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed a large-scale operation killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran. The IDF stated Khamenei was responsible for years of repression and aimed to destroy Israel, leading a terror axis. His elimination marks the end of a significant chapter, according to the military. Iran's government acknowledged the US-Israeli strikes shortly after.

stories.title: 'Full readiness to handle situation': UAE intercepts 137 missiles, 209 drones fired from Iran
India’s CBSE postpones class 10 and 12 board exams in Middle East; New dates to be announced
stories.summary: CBSE has postponed Class 10 and 12 board exams scheduled for March 2, 2026, in several Middle Eastern nations due to escalating geopolitical tensions. The decision prioritizes student and staff safety amidst regional instability, with new dates to be announced after a review on March 3. The board also debunked a fake circular claiming permanent cancellation of exams.

stories.title: Who is Ali Larijani? Khamenei’s trusted adviser and key figure in Iran’s leadership
stories.summary: Following Supreme Leader Khamenei's killing, Iran's top security official Ali Larijani vowed retaliation against the US and announced plans for a transitional leadership council. Larijani, a powerful figure with extensive experience, will oversee the immediate political management and security response during this critical juncture for the Islamic Republic.

stories.title: Who is Mojtaba Khamenei? Ayatollah’s son tipped to succeed Iran’s Supreme Leader
stories.summary: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's reported death in US-Israeli strikes has created a leadership vacuum in Iran, with his son Mojtaba emerging as a potential successor. Mojtaba, an influential but opaque figure with strong ties to the IRGC, faces constitutional hurdles to the top post.

stories.title: Dr. Abdullah Al Rabeeah: Surgeon who turned Saudi Arabia into global hub for conjoined twins surgery
Over 700 flights cancelled today: UAE, India and global airlines disrupted as US-Israel-Iran war escalates
stories.summary: Global aviation is in turmoil on March 1, 2026, as escalating US, Israel, and Iran conflict forces widespread airspace closures. Over 700 flights were cancelled by afternoon, with thousands of passengers stranded. Major carriers like Emirates and Air India suspended operations, impacting key transit hubs and leading to soaring fare prices.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran with ‘force never seen before’; MEA issues advisory — Key points
stories.summary: Iran launched retaliatory strikes against US and Israeli targets following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in a US-Israel operation. Key Iranian military leaders were also reported dead. The conflict has triggered widespread flight cancellations and airspace restrictions, causing significant travel disruptions across the region.

stories.title: 'Delivering decisive action as directed': US releases new videos of strikes on Iran
